Checked against the standard library's docs, as spec §22 asks: `Request.add_unredirected_header` adds a header that a redirected request doesn't carry; an `HTTPRedirectHandler.redirect_request` that returns None makes the default error handler raise `HTTPError(code)`, as `alerts.py`'s `_NoRedirect` relies on; `build_opener` leaves out a default handler when a subclass of it is passed, so `_HTTPHandler` and `_HTTPSHandler` replace them; `HTTPResponse.read1(n)` returns at most `n` bytes from one read, and an empty result at a premature end.

```python
"""The Plaud client: direct, read-only HTTP against Plaud's public third-party API (stage 2b spec
§10.1).

Copied from audio-router's `src/audio_router/archive/sources/plaud.py` at commit 64612df: Dan's
own code, relicensed MIT for this repo (main spec §19). The edits, each from §10.1:
- **IDs are opaque.** audio-router's `FILE_ID_RE` filter rejected Plaud's `of_<32 hex>` IDs, which
  is why its sync stopped. Nothing here checks an ID against a pattern. Every request uses the ID
  exactly as the newest listing gave it; the canonical form is only for comparing.
- **Only reads.** One request function sends `GET`. The refresh `POST` arrives with the token store
  in Phase 2 (spikes S1, S2, S4); until then a `TokenSource` supplies the access token and its
  refresh, replacing audio-router's call to the vendor CLI.
- **Redirects and the token.** API calls refuse every redirect, as `alerts.py` does. Authorization
  goes only to the API host, as an unredirected header. Presigned links (the audio, and blocks
  behind a `data_link`) are fetched without it, must be `https`, and may follow a redirect only to
  another `https` URL. Plain `http` is allowed only to the loopback, and only while the API base is
  the loopback too: that is the tests' fake (2b phase 1 plan, decision 7).
- **Nothing secret or personal leaves it.** Every error is one of this module's classes, with a
  fixed message, raised `from None` outside the handler that caught the cause, so no chained
  exception carries a URL, a token or a body (some `urllib` errors hold the whole URL). A block
  that fails records its error's class name, never `str(exc)`. A Plaud ID is shown only as
  `id_hash`.
- **Timeouts:** 10 seconds to connect, 60 to read. A download also has a stall rule: no bytes for
  60 seconds (the read timeout), or under 50 KB/s on average after its first minute. Past that
  minute, staying above the average also bounds the whole download by Content-Length / MIN_RATE,
  which is §10.1's ceiling scaled from Content-Length.

Phase 2 sets `PAGE_SIZE` from S5 and adds pacing, the budget and backoff from S5 and S10 (§10.2):
this copy makes one call when asked and never waits.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import http.client
import ipaddress
import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Callable
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Protocol
from urllib.parse import SplitResult, quote, urlsplit
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from recordings import __version__
from recordings.config import ConfigError
from recordings.refs import canonical_plaud_id

API_BASE = "https://platform.plaud.ai/developer/api"  # as copied
LIST_PATH = "/open/third-party/files/"
FILE_PATH = "/open/third-party/files/{}"
PAGE_SIZE = 100  # as copied (the API rejects anything under 10). Phase 2: S5, S10.
CONNECT_TIMEOUT = 10.0
READ_TIMEOUT = 60.0
STALL_SECONDS = 60.0  # no bytes for this long
MIN_RATE = 50_000  # bytes per second on average after the first minute
USER_AGENT = f"recordings/{__version__}"  # bare urllib's default gets a flat 403 from this API
_CHUNK = 64 * 1024
_LOOPBACK_NAMES = frozenset({"localhost"})
_REDIRECTS = frozenset({301, 302, 303, 307, 308})
_LIST_KEYS = ("data", "data_list", "files", "items", "list")


class PlaudError(Exception):
    """Every error the client raises: a fixed message per class (spec §15.6), raised `from None`,
    so no URL, token or body travels with it."""

    message = "Plaud error"

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__(self.message)


class PlaudAuthError(PlaudError):
    message = "sign-in needed"


class PlaudForbidden(PlaudError):
    message = "Plaud refused access (403)"


class PlaudUnavailable(PlaudError):
    message = "Plaud unavailable"


class PlaudOffline(PlaudError):
    message = "offline"


class PlaudRateLimited(PlaudError):
    message = "rate limited"

    def __init__(self, retry_after: float | None = None) -> None:
        super().__init__()
        self.retry_after = retry_after


class PlaudBadResponse(PlaudError):
    message = "Plaud's answer couldn't be read"


class PlaudRedirectRefused(PlaudError):
    message = "Plaud answered with a redirect, which is never followed"


class PlaudLinkRefused(PlaudError):
    message = "a link from Plaud was refused"


class IncompleteDownload(PlaudError):
    message = "the download was short, empty or stalled"


class TokenSource(Protocol):
    def access_token(self) -> str:
        """The current access token; PlaudAuthError when there is none."""
        ...

    def refresh(self, rejected: str) -> str:
        """After a 401 on `rejected`: a new access token, or PlaudAuthError."""
        ...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Listed:
    """One row of the list endpoint: metadata only, no content."""

    listed_id: str  # exactly as the listing gave it
    title: str | None  # None: the row had no title field
    created_at: datetime | None
    start_at: datetime | None
    duration_ms: int | None
    serial: str = ""

    @property
    def canonical_id(self) -> str:
        return canonical_plaud_id(self.listed_id)

    @property
    def recorded_at(self) -> datetime | None:
        """Best available capture time. start_at is the capture time for device recordings; for
        uploads it is the upload moment, which is why S12 checks it (§18)."""
        return self.start_at or self.created_at


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Page:
    rows: tuple[Listed, ...]
    malformed: int  # rows with no ID or no title field (§11.2 counts them)


def _parse_dt(value: object) -> datetime | None:
    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value:
        return None
    try:
        dt = datetime.fromisoformat(value)  # 3.11 and later read a trailing Z
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return dt.replace(tzinfo=UTC) if dt.tzinfo is None else dt


def _duration(value: object) -> int | None:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int | float):
        return None
    return int(value)


def _is_loopback(host: str | None) -> bool:
    if not host:
        return False
    if host in _LOOPBACK_NAMES:
        return True
    try:
        return ipaddress.ip_address(host).is_loopback
    except ValueError:
        return False


def _plain_url(url: object) -> bool:
    """Visible ASCII, no space: the URL checked is the URL sent (urlsplit drops a tab or a newline
    that the request would keep), and a host can't be a look-alike."""
    return isinstance(url, str) and url.isascii() and url.isprintable() and " " not in url


def _split(url: object) -> SplitResult | None:
    """The URL's parts, or None unless it is plain, with a host, a numeric port if any, and no
    user name or password."""
    if not _plain_url(url):
        return None
    try:
        parts = urlsplit(str(url))
        _ = parts.port  # a port that isn't a number raises ValueError
    except ValueError:  # a malformed IPv6 address, or port
        return None
    return parts if parts.hostname and "@" not in parts.netloc else None


def _loopback_http(api_base: str) -> bool:
    parts = _split(api_base)
    return parts is not None and parts.scheme == "http" and _is_loopback(parts.hostname)


def check_api_base(url: object) -> str:
    """`[plaud] api_base`: https://, or http:// to the loopback for tests (§10.1), with no query
    or fragment, since paths are added to its end. The error names the setting, never the URL."""
    parts = _split(url)
    if (
        parts is None
        or any(c in str(url) for c in "?#")
        or not (
            parts.scheme == "https" or (parts.scheme == "http" and _is_loopback(parts.hostname))
        )
    ):
        raise ConfigError(
            "[plaud] api_base must be an https:// URL in plain ASCII (http:// only to this "
            "machine's loopback), with no user name, password, query (?) or fragment (#)"
        )
    return str(url).rstrip("/")


def check_link(url: object, *, api_base: str) -> str:
    """A presigned link from Plaud: https, in visible ASCII; plain http only to the loopback while
    `api_base` is the loopback too (decision 7). Otherwise PlaudLinkRefused, without the URL: a
    link may carry a signature that grants Dan's audio."""
    parts = _split(url)
    secure = parts is not None and parts.scheme == "https"
    test_http = (
        parts is not None
        and parts.scheme == "http"
        and _is_loopback(parts.hostname)
        and _loopback_http(api_base)
    )
    if not (secure or test_http):
        raise PlaudLinkRefused() from None
    return str(url)


def id_hash(plaud_id: str) -> str:
    """The only form a Plaud ID is shown in: 8 hex of the SHA-256 of its canonical form (§10.1)."""
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_plaud_id(plaud_id).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:8]


class _HTTPConnection(http.client.HTTPConnection):
    """Connects within CONNECT_TIMEOUT (the opener's timeout), then reads with READ_TIMEOUT."""

    def connect(self) -> None:
        super().connect()
        self.sock.settimeout(READ_TIMEOUT)


class _HTTPSConnection(http.client.HTTPSConnection):
    def connect(self) -> None:
        super().connect()  # the TCP connect and the TLS handshake, within CONNECT_TIMEOUT
        self.sock.settimeout(READ_TIMEOUT)


class _HTTPHandler(urllib.request.HTTPHandler):
    def http_open(self, req: urllib.request.Request) -> http.client.HTTPResponse:
        return self.do_open(_HTTPConnection, req)


class _HTTPSHandler(urllib.request.HTTPSHandler):
    def https_open(self, req: urllib.request.Request) -> http.client.HTTPResponse:
        return self.do_open(_HTTPSConnection, req, context=self._context)


class _NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    """An API call is never redirected: it carries the token (alerts.py's `_NoRedirect`)."""

    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None  # HTTPDefaultErrorHandler raises HTTPError(code): PlaudRedirectRefused


class _HttpsRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    """A presigned link may be redirected only to another https URL (§10.1)."""

    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        parts = _split(newurl)
        if parts is None or parts.scheme != "https":
            fp.close()
            raise PlaudLinkRefused() from None
        return super().redirect_request(req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl)


def _opener(redirects: urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler) -> urllib.request.OpenerDirector:
    """Proxies from the environment only, and only for https, as alerts.py's: through one, a
    request travels in a CONNECT tunnel and the proxy sees the host name alone. The default
    handler would also ask macOS's system configuration, which starts threads that never end."""
    proxies = urllib.request.getproxies_environment()
    return urllib.request.build_opener(
        urllib.request.ProxyHandler({k: v for k, v in proxies.items() if k == "https"}),
        _HTTPHandler,
        _HTTPSHandler,
        redirects,
    )


_API_OPENER = _opener(_NoRedirect())
_LINK_OPENER = _opener(_HttpsRedirect())


def _retry_after(headers: Any) -> float | None:
    value = headers.get("Retry-After") if headers is not None else None
    return float(value) if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip().isdigit() else None


def _from_http(exc: urllib.error.HTTPError) -> PlaudError:
    code = exc.code
    if code in _REDIRECTS:
        return PlaudRedirectRefused()
    if code == 401:
        return PlaudAuthError()
    if code == 403:
        return PlaudForbidden()
    if code == 429:
        return PlaudRateLimited(_retry_after(exc.headers))
    if code == 408 or code >= 500:
        return PlaudUnavailable()
    return PlaudBadResponse()


def _from_transport(exc: BaseException, short: type[PlaudError]) -> PlaudError:
    """A failure below HTTP (§10.2): a body cut short is `short`; no connection at all (refused,
    unreachable, no DNS) is "offline"; a timeout, a reset, TLS or a broken reply is "Plaud
    unavailable"."""
    reason = exc.reason if isinstance(exc, urllib.error.URLError) else exc
    if isinstance(reason, http.client.IncompleteRead):
        return short()
    if isinstance(
        reason, TimeoutError | ConnectionResetError | ssl.SSLError | http.client.HTTPException
    ):
        return PlaudUnavailable()
    if isinstance(reason, OSError):
        return PlaudOffline()
    return PlaudUnavailable()


class PlaudClient:
    """Thin, read-only HTTP client: one request function, fixed errors, nothing logged."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        tokens: TokenSource,
        *,
        api_base: str = API_BASE,
        monotonic: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic,
        stall_seconds: float = STALL_SECONDS,
        min_rate: int = MIN_RATE,
    ) -> None:
        self.tokens = tokens
        self.api_base = check_api_base(api_base)
        self.monotonic = monotonic
        self.stall_seconds = stall_seconds
        self.min_rate = min_rate

    # -- the one request function: GET only -------------------------------------------------
    def _get(
        self,
        url: str,
        *,
        token: str | None,
        short: type[PlaudError],
    ) -> bytes:
        request = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET")
        request.add_header("User-Agent", USER_AGENT)
        opener = _LINK_OPENER
        if token is not None:
            # Unredirected: never copied onto a redirect, which _NoRedirect refuses anyway.
            request.add_unredirected_header("Authorization", f"Bearer {token}")
            request.add_header("Accept", "application/json, text/plain, */*")
            opener = _API_OPENER
        error: PlaudError | None = None
        try:
            with opener.open(request, timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT) as response:
                return response.read()  # a body shorter than Content-Length raises IncompleteRead
        except PlaudError as exc:  # a refused link redirect, raised in _HttpsRedirect
            error = exc
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            error = _from_http(exc)
            exc.close()
        except (urllib.error.URLError, http.client.HTTPException, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            error = _from_transport(exc, short)
        raise error from None

    def get_json(self, path: str) -> Any:
        """GET `api_base + path` with the access token. A 401 asks the token source for a new
        token once and tries once more; a second 401 is PlaudAuthError."""
        if not path.startswith("/") or not _plain_url(path):
            raise ValueError("get_json takes a path on the API host")
        url = self.api_base + path
        token = self.tokens.access_token()
        try:
            body: bytes | None = self._get(url, token=token, short=PlaudBadResponse)
        except PlaudAuthError:
            body = None
        if body is None:  # a 401: one refresh, then one more try
            body = self._get(url, token=self.tokens.refresh(token), short=PlaudBadResponse)
        try:
            return json.loads(body)
        except ValueError:  # broken JSON, an HTML page, bytes that aren't UTF-8
            raise PlaudBadResponse() from None

    # -- endpoints -------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def list_page(self, page: int, page_size: int = PAGE_SIZE) -> Page:
        """One page of the listing. No ID is checked against a pattern: IDs are opaque. A caller
        pages until an empty page, never stopping at a short one: a server that clamps page sizes
        would otherwise end the listing early, and erase what it never listed (§11.2)."""
        payload = self.get_json(f"{LIST_PATH}?page={int(page)}&page_size={int(page_size)}")
        if isinstance(payload, list):
            batch = payload
        elif isinstance(payload, dict):
            batch = next((payload[k] for k in _LIST_KEYS if isinstance(payload.get(k), list)), None)
        else:
            batch = None
        if batch is None:
            raise PlaudBadResponse()  # an HTML page or the wrong shape is never an empty account
        rows, malformed = [], 0
        for row in batch:
            listed_id = row.get("id") if isinstance(row, dict) else None
            if not isinstance(listed_id, str) or not listed_id.strip():
                # A missing or renamed `id` must never become "": audio-router's lesson.
                malformed += 1
                continue
            title = row.get("name")
            if not isinstance(title, str):
                malformed += 1
                title = None
            rows.append(
                Listed(
                    listed_id=listed_id.strip(),
                    title=title,
                    created_at=_parse_dt(row.get("created_at")),
                    start_at=_parse_dt(row.get("start_at")),
                    duration_ms=_duration(row.get("duration")),
                    serial=str(row.get("serial_number") or ""),
                )
            )
        return Page(rows=tuple(rows), malformed=malformed)

    def envelope(self, listed_id: str) -> dict:
        """The whole files/{id} answer, for the ID exactly as listed, with block bodies behind a
        `data_link` fetched at once (their links expire within 300 seconds). A block that fails
        records its error's class name in place, so one unreachable block costs only itself."""
        env = self.get_json(FILE_PATH.format(quote(listed_id, safe="")))
        if not isinstance(env, dict):
            raise PlaudBadResponse()
        enriched: list[str] = []
        for section in ("source_list", "note_list"):
            blocks = env.get(section)
            for block in blocks if isinstance(blocks, list) else []:
                if not isinstance(block, dict):
                    continue
                content = block.get("data_content")
                link = block.get("data_link")
                if (isinstance(content, str) and content.strip()) or not link:
                    continue
                try:
                    block["data_content"] = self.fetch_link(link).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                except PlaudError as exc:
                    block["_data_link_error"] = type(exc).__name__
                    continue
                block["_fetched_from_data_link"] = True
                enriched.append(str(block.get("data_type") or "?"))
        meta = env.setdefault("_meta", {})
        if isinstance(meta, dict):
            meta["enriched_from_links"] = enriched
        return env

    def fetch_link(self, url: str) -> bytes:
        """A presigned link's body: checked by check_link, sent without Authorization."""
        return self._get(
            check_link(url, api_base=self.api_base), token=None, short=IncompleteDownload
        )

    def download(self, url: str, dest: Path) -> int:
        """Stream a presigned link to `dest`. Complete as well as atomic: a body that isn't
        exactly Content-Length bytes, an empty one, one with no Content-Length, or a stall, is
        IncompleteDownload, and no file is left. CPython's read(amt) returns b"" at a premature
        end rather than raising, which once let audio-router rename a 100-byte fragment into
        place, so the count is compared here (S11 checks the storage host sends the length)."""
        link = check_link(url, api_base=self.api_base)
        dest = Path(dest)
        dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        part = dest.with_name(dest.name + ".part")
        request = urllib.request.Request(link, method="GET")
        request.add_header("User-Agent", USER_AGENT)
        error: PlaudError | None = None
        written = 0
        try:
            with (
                _LINK_OPENER.open(request, timeout=CONNECT_TIMEOUT) as response,
                part.open("wb") as fh,
            ):
                declared = response.headers.get("Content-Length")
                expected = int(declared) if declared and declared.isdigit() else None
                start = self.monotonic()
                while chunk := response.read1(_CHUNK):
                    fh.write(chunk)
                    written += len(chunk)
                    elapsed = self.monotonic() - start
                    if elapsed > self.stall_seconds and written / elapsed < self.min_rate:
                        raise IncompleteDownload()
            if expected is None or written != expected or written == 0:
                raise IncompleteDownload()
            os.replace(part, dest)
            return written
        except PlaudError as exc:
            error = exc
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            error = _from_http(exc)
            exc.close()
        except (urllib.error.URLError, http.client.HTTPException, OSError, ValueError) as exc:
            error = _from_transport(exc, IncompleteDownload)
        finally:
            if error is not None or not dest.exists():
                part.unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise error from None


def stamp_meta(listed: Listed, tz_name: str) -> dict:
    """Resolve the recording time once, and record how (audio-router's keys), with `tool`, which
    marks a snapshot written by this app (`_meta.tool == "recordings"`, the gate's test, §11.6).
    Persisted into the snapshot so a later reindex reads it back rather than re-deriving it from a
    time zone that may since have changed; `time_source` exists because a missing time is
    otherwise indistinguishable from midnight."""
    tz = ZoneInfo(tz_name)
    source = "start_at" if listed.start_at else ("created_at" if listed.created_at else None)
    utc = listed.recorded_at
    local = utc.astimezone(tz) if utc else None
    return {
        "recorded_at_utc": utc.isoformat() if utc else None,
        "recorded_at_local": local.isoformat() if local else None,
        "stamp": local.strftime("%Y-%m-%d-%H%M") if local else None,
        "timezone": tz_name,
        "time_source": source,
        "tool": "recordings",
    }
```

```python
NORMAL = f"{0x42:032x}"  # in the archive, untagged
PRIVATE = f"{0xA7:032x}"  # in the archive, tagged private
CONSENTED = f"{0xC0:032x}"  # on the consent list
TOKEN = "synthetic-access-token-0042"
TITLES = ("Synthetic 042 meeting with Ada", "Synthetic consent-listed", "Synthetic 7 private")
WORDS_SAID = "Synthetic words nobody may print"


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def spike():
    """The script, loaded by path. It is registered first: its dataclasses look their module up."""
    path = REPO / "scripts" / "plaud_spike.py"
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("plaud_spike", path)
    module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
    sys.modules["plaud_spike"] = module
    spec.loader.exec_module(module)
    yield module
    del sys.modules["plaud_spike"]


def _plaud(ref: str) -> tuple[RawSource, ...]:
    return (RawSource(kind="plaud", ref=ref, added_at=T0, payload=b'{"id": 1}'),)


@pytest.fixture
def env(tmp_path, writer, make_incoming, plaud_server, monkeypatch, spike):
    """A synthetic archive (one plain recording, one private), a consent list, a config pointing
    the spike at both and at the fake, and a session token file in the spike folder."""
    writer.add(make_incoming(sources=_plaud("of_" + NORMAL)))

    )


def _guard(spike):
    cfg = load_config(os.environ)
    return spike.build_guard(cfg, Archive(cfg.archive_path))


def test_the_guard_refuses_a_consent_listed_id_and_counts_it(env, spike):
    guard = _guard(spike)
    assert guard.consent == {CONSENTED}
    assert not guard.allows("OF_" + CONSENTED.upper(), "Week 4")
    assert guard.allows(NORMAL, "Week 4")
    assert guard.refused == collections.Counter(consent=1)
    assert guard.report() == "refused: 1 (consent 1)"


def test_the_guard_refuses_a_private_tagged_recording_and_counts_it(env, spike):
    guard = _guard(spike)
    assert guard.private_ids == {PRIVATE}  # the recording's ref was upper case: canonical here
    assert not guard.allows(PRIVATE, "Week 4") and not guard.allows("of_" + PRIVATE, "Week 4")
    assert guard.report() == "refused: 2 (private 2)"


def test_the_guard_refuses_a_keep_out_title_unless_it_is_the_own_clip(env, spike):
    guard = _guard(spike)
    assert not guard.allows(NORMAL, "NoArchive: synthetic")
    assert guard.allows(NORMAL, "NoArchive: synthetic", own_clip=True)
    env.configure('keep_out_word = "skipme"\n')
    guard = _guard(spike)
    assert guard.words == ("skipme", "noarchive")  # the default stays: erring towards refusing
    assert not guard.allows(NORMAL, "skipme 7") and not guard.allows(NORMAL, "noarchive 7")
    assert guard.report() == "refused: 2 (keep-out 2)"


def test_the_guard_refuses_a_pattern_title_even_for_the_own_clip(env, spike):
    # why: decision 24. --own-clip skips the keep-out check and nothing else.
    guard = _guard(spike)
    assert guard.patterns == DEFAULT_AUTO_PRIVATE
    assert not guard.allows(NORMAL, "Private: synthetic", own_clip=True)
    assert not guard.allows(NORMAL, "ｐｒｉｖａｔｅ notes", own_clip=True)  # folded, as §13.1 says
    assert not guard.allows(NORMAL, None, own_clip=True)  # no title: it can't be checked
    assert guard.report() == "refused: 3 (pattern 3)"


@pytest.mark.parametrize(

def _serve_account(fake) -> None:
    rows = [
        {"id": "of_" + NORMAL, "name": TITLES[0], "start_at": "2026-08-01T16:00:00Z"},
        {"id": CONSENTED.upper(), "name": TITLES[1], "start_at": "2026-08-02T16:00:00Z"},
        {"id": "of_" + PRIVATE, "name": TITLES[2], "start_at": "2026-08-03T16:00:00Z"},
    ]

    def listing(query):
        return Response(
            200, json.dumps({"data_list": rows if query["page"] == ["1"] else []}).encode()
        )

    fake.route("GET", LIST_PATH, listing)
    segments = [{"content": WORDS_SAID, "start_time": 0, "end_time": 900, "embeddingKey": "ek-1"}]
    block = fake.link("transcript", json.dumps(segments).encode())
    envelope = {
        "id": "of_" + NORMAL,
        "name": TITLES[0],
        "presigned_url": f"{fake.storage_url}/audio.mp3?X-Amz-Expires=300",
        "source_list": [{"data_type": "transaction", "data_content": "", "data_link": block}],
        "note_list": [
            {"data_type": "auto_sum_note", "data_tab_name": "Summary", "data_content": WORDS_SAID}
        ],
    }
    body = json.dumps(envelope).encode()
    fake.route("GET", FILE_PATH.format("of_" + NORMAL), lambda q: Response(200, body))


def test_nothing_printed_holds_a_title_a_token_or_a_whole_id(env, spike, capsys):
    # why: §18's print list. A spike's output is read aloud in a session and may be pasted
    # anywhere: counts, yes or no, times, field names and 8-hex prefixes only.
    _serve_account(env.fake)
    assert spike.main(["s5", "--home", str(env.home)]) == 0
    s5 = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "pass 1: 3 IDs, 0 repeats, 0 malformed, 2 pages" in s5
    assert "same ID set: yes" in s5
    assert spike.main(["s8", "--home", str(env.home), "--id", NORMAL, "--id", CONSENTED]) == 0
    s8 = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert f"{spike.short(NORMAL)}: part transcript: matched yes" in s8
    assert f"{spike.short(CONSENTED)}: refused by the guard" in s8
    assert s8.rstrip().endswith("refused: 1 (consent 1)")
    out = s5 + s8
    for secret in (*TITLES, TOKEN, WORDS_SAID, "Summary", "ek-1", "X-Amz", env.fake.storage_url):
        assert secret not in out, secret
    for whole in (NORMAL, PRIVATE, CONSENTED):
        assert whole not in out.lower(), whole
    assert {r.method for r in env.fake.requests} == {"GET"}


def test_the_spike_folder_must_be_0700_and_outside_the_archive_state_and_plaud(
    env, spike, monkeypatch
):
    folder = spike.spike_folder(env.home)
    assert folder == env.home / "spike" and stat.S_IMODE(folder.stat().st_mode) == 0o700
    folder.chmod(0o755)
    with pytest.raises(spike.SpikeRefused, match="must be 0700"):
        spike.spike_folder(env.home)
    folder.chmod(0o700)

    plaud = env.tmp / "plaud"

    env.configure(f'[backup]\nextra_paths = ["{env.tmp / "backed-up"}"]\n')
    for home in (env.writer.root, env.writer.state.path, plaud, env.tmp / "backed-up"):
        with pytest.raises(spike.SpikeRefused, match="must be outside"):
            spike.spike_folder(home)
        assert not (home / "spike").exists()
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the code,** `scripts/plaud_spike.py`: the guard, the spike folder, and each spike's steps and print list from spec §18, S1 to S12. S2 and S4 POST to the token URL (the only POSTs, on purpose, at Dan's word); S10 and S11's raw GETs read the header names and the `Range` answer the client keeps to itself.

```python
"""The Plaud spikes (stage 2b spec §18): supervised test plans, each run with Dan in a session.

    uv run python scripts/plaud_spike.py <spike> [--home DIR] [--token-file FILE] [--id ID]...
        [--token-url URL] [--own-clip]

It imports `recordings`, so it runs in the workspace, with no PEP 723 block (2b phase 1 plan,
decision 24). Never in CI and never by an agent: only in Dan's sessions A (s1, s2, s4, s3), B (s5,
s7, s8, s10, s12, s11) and C (s9), as runbook section 1c says. Its tests run it against fakes.

**The guard** runs before any Plaud call. The consent list is read fail-closed: a consent stop
refuses the whole spike, exit 78. A spike that fetches `files/{id}` or downloads audio refuses any
consent-listed ID, any recording tagged private in the archive, any title a keep-out word matches
(S9's own clip aside: `--own-clip`), and any title an auto-private pattern matches, the own clip
included (decision 24). A row with no title can't be checked, so it is refused as well. Every
spike ends by printing how many it refused, by reason.

**What it prints** is each spike's §18 print list: counts, yes or no, times, status codes, field
names and `short()` prefixes (8 hex of a SHA-256). Never a token, a title, transcript text or a
whole Plaud ID. An error line names an exception's class, never its text.

**The spike folder** is `$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike`, mode 0700, outside the archive, the state folder,
the index, `/plaud` and every backup path. The session's sign-in (a temporary HOME, `--token-file`)
lives in it, and so does anything a spike downloads, deleted at once. Dan deletes the folder at the
end of the session (runbook 1c). A spike never refreshes the sign-in behind Dan's back: S2 and S4
refresh on purpose, at the token URL S1 finds (`--token-url`, https only).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import base64
import collections
import json
import os
import stat
import sys
import tempfile
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from collections.abc import Callable, Iterable
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import UTC, datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from recordings.archive import Archive, sha256_file
from recordings.config import Config, ConfigError, load_config
from recordings.ids import ID_RE
from recordings.models import Recording, is_private
from recordings.plaud.client import (
    API_BASE,
    FILE_PATH,
    LIST_PATH,
    PAGE_SIZE,
    Listed,
    PlaudAuthError,
    PlaudClient,
    PlaudError,
    check_api_base,
    check_link,
    id_hash,
)
from recordings.plaud.consent import ConsentListError, consent_list_path
from recordings.plaud.keepout import DEFAULT_WORD, fold, keep_out_match, read_consent, valid_word
from recordings.plaud.normalise import part_hashes, transcript_rows
from recordings.plaud.reconcile import matches_auto_private, patterns_from_config
from recordings.refs import canonical_plaud_id

SPIKES = ("s1", "s2", "s3", "s4", "s5", "s7", "s8", "s9", "s10", "s11", "s12")
REASONS = ("consent", "private", "keep-out", "pattern")
EXIT_REFUSED = 78
PLAUD_MOUNT = Path("/plaud")
PAUSE = 60.0  # S5 and S8: "a minute apart"
MOMENT = 5.0  # S9: "a moment apart"
PAGE_CAP = 500  # §11.2: a listing that reaches it is bad
TIMEOUT = 60.0
SIZES = (5, 20, 50, 100, 500)  # S5's page sizes
_CODE_CHARS = frozenset("abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_")
_LIST_KEYS = ("data", "data_list", "files", "items", "list")
sleep = time.sleep  # the tests replace it: a spike's pauses are real only in Dan's sessions


class SpikeRefused(Exception):
    """A fixed phrase: main() prints it and exits 78."""


@dataclass
class Guard:
    consent: frozenset[str]  # canonical IDs; a consent stop raises SpikeRefused before any call
    private_ids: frozenset[str]  # canonical Plaud IDs of archive recordings tagged private
    words: tuple[str, ...]
    patterns: tuple[str, ...]
    refused: collections.Counter[str] = field(default_factory=collections.Counter)

    def allows(self, plaud_id: str, title: str | None, *, own_clip: bool = False) -> bool:
        """Whether a spike may fetch or download this recording. `own_clip` (S9's clip) skips the
        keep-out check, and nothing else."""
        canonical = canonical_plaud_id(plaud_id)
        if canonical in self.consent:
            reason = "consent"
        elif canonical in self.private_ids:
            reason = "private"
        elif title is None:
            reason = "pattern"  # no title to check: refused, the safe way
        elif not own_clip and keep_out_match(title, self.words):
            reason = "keep-out"
        elif matches_auto_private([title, fold(title)], self.patterns):
            reason = "pattern"
        else:
            return True
        self.refused[reason] += 1
        return False

    def report(self) -> str:
        total = sum(self.refused.values())
        if not total:
            return "refused: 0"
        parts = ", ".join(f"{r} {self.refused[r]}" for r in REASONS if self.refused[r])
        return f"refused: {total} ({parts})"


def short(value: str) -> str:
    """8 hex of the SHA-256: the only form an ID, or any other value, is printed in. A Plaud ID is
    hashed in its canonical form (`client.id_hash`), so both of its forms print alike."""
    return id_hash(value)


def _hex32(value: str) -> bool:
    return len(value) == 32 and all(c in "0123456789abcdef" for c in value)


def _plaud_ids(rec: Recording) -> list[str]:
    return [canonical_plaud_id(s.ref) for s in rec.sources if s.kind == "plaud"]


def _section(cfg: Config, name: str) -> dict:
    value = cfg.data.get(name, {})
    return value if isinstance(value, dict) else {}


def build_guard(cfg: Config, archive: Archive) -> Guard:
    """The consent list (fail-closed), the archive's private recordings, the keep-out words (the
    configured one and the default, erring towards refusing) and the auto-private patterns."""
    try:
        path = consent_list_path(cfg.data)
    except ConsentListError:
        path = None
    consent = read_consent(path)
    if consent.stop is not None:
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused before any call: {consent.stop}")
    recordings = list(archive.iter_recordings())
    if archive.problems:
        raise SpikeRefused(
            f"refused before any call: {len(archive.problems)} recordings in the archive can't "
            "be read, so it can't tell which are private (run `recordings validate`)"
        )
    word = _section(cfg, "plaud").get("keep_out_word", DEFAULT_WORD)
    if not valid_word(word):
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: configuration: `keep_out_word` is invalid")
    private_ids = frozenset(pid for rec in recordings if is_private(rec) for pid in _plaud_ids(rec))
    words = tuple(dict.fromkeys([word, DEFAULT_WORD]))
    return Guard(consent.ids, private_ids, words, patterns_from_config(cfg.data))


def _kept_apart(cfg: Config) -> list[Path]:
    """The folders the spike folder stays out of: the archive, the state folder, the index,
    /plaud, and the backup's paths (the archive and the state folder are backed up too)."""
    backup = _section(cfg, "backup")
    named = [backup.get("restore_scratch"), backup.get("cache_dir")]
    extra = backup.get("extra_paths", [])
    named += extra if isinstance(extra, list) else []
    paths = [cfg.archive_path, cfg.state_path, PLAUD_MOUNT]
    paths += [Path(p).expanduser() for p in named if isinstance(p, str) and p]
    if cfg.index_path is not None:
        paths.append(cfg.index_path.parent)
    return [Path(p).expanduser().absolute().resolve() for p in paths if p is not None]


def spike_folder(home: Path) -> Path:
    """`$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike` at 0700, made if missing. Refused when it is wider than 0700, or
    inside (or holding) the archive, the state folder, the index, `/plaud` or a backup path."""
    folder = Path(home).expanduser().absolute() / "spike"
    resolved = folder.resolve()
    for kept in _kept_apart(load_config(os.environ)):
        if resolved.is_relative_to(kept) or kept.is_relative_to(resolved):
            raise SpikeRefused(
                "refused: the spike folder must be outside the archive, the state folder, the "
                f"index, {PLAUD_MOUNT} and every backup path"
            )
    folder.mkdir(mode=0o700, parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    if stat.S_IMODE(folder.stat().st_mode) & 0o077:
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: the spike folder must be 0700: chmod 700 {folder}")
    return folder


class FileTokens:
    """The session's sign-in, read from --token-file: the vendor CLI's token file, whose access
    token audio-router read as "access_token". A spike never refreshes behind Dan's back, so a
    401 is reported as it is."""

    def __init__(self, path: Path) -> None:
        self.path = path

    def data(self) -> dict:
        try:
            data = json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        except (OSError, ValueError):
            raise PlaudAuthError() from None
        if not isinstance(data, dict):
            raise PlaudAuthError()
        return data

    def access_token(self) -> str:
        token = self.data().get("access_token")
        if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
            raise PlaudAuthError()
        return token

    def refresh(self, rejected: str) -> str:
        raise PlaudAuthError()


@dataclass
class Session:
    args: argparse.Namespace
    cfg: Config
    archive: Archive
    guard: Guard
    folder: Path
    tokens: FileTokens
    client: PlaudClient
    monotonic: Callable[[], float] = time.monotonic
    now: Callable[[], datetime] = field(default=lambda: datetime.now(UTC))


# -- printing --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def say(*parts: object) -> None:
    print(*parts, flush=True)


def _error(exc: BaseException) -> str:
    return type(exc).__name__


def _yes(value: object) -> str:
    return "yes" if value else "no"


def _names(keys: Iterable[object]) -> str:
    return ", ".join(sorted(str(k) for k in keys)) or "none"


def _code(reply: dict) -> str:
    """The OAuth `error` code, only when it looks like one (never its description)."""
    code = reply.get("error")
    if isinstance(code, str) and 0 < len(code) <= 40 and set(code) <= _CODE_CHARS:
        return f", error {code}"
    return ""


def _time(value: object) -> str:
    """An expiry as a UTC time, from epoch seconds (or milliseconds) or ISO 8601; a smaller number
    is a duration in seconds. Anything else is only "present"."""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "present"
    if isinstance(value, int | float):
        if value > 10**9:
            seconds = value / 1000 if value > 10**12 else value
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(seconds, UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
        return f"{int(value)} s"
    if isinstance(value, str):
        try:
            when = datetime.fromisoformat(value)
        except ValueError:
            return "present"
        when = when if when.tzinfo else when.replace(tzinfo=UTC)
        return when.astimezone(UTC).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M UTC")
    return "present"


def _expires(url: object) -> str:
    """A presigned link's X-Amz-Expires, as seconds, or "unknown"."""
    if not isinstance(url, str):
        return "unknown"
    values = urllib.parse.parse_qs(urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).query).get("X-Amz-Expires", [])
    return f"{values[0]} s" if values and values[0].isdigit() else "unknown"


# -- reading Plaud ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def _batch(payload: Any) -> tuple[str, list]:
    if isinstance(payload, list):
        return "a list", payload
    if isinstance(payload, dict):
        key = next((k for k in _LIST_KEYS if isinstance(payload.get(k), list)), None)
        return f"an object with keys {_names(payload)}", payload[key] if key else []
    return "neither a list nor an object", []


@dataclass
class Listing:
    rows: list[Listed]
    malformed: int
    pages: int

    def census(self) -> str:
        forms = collections.Counter(
            "of_"
            if row.listed_id.lower().startswith("of_")
            else "bare"
            if _hex32(row.listed_id.lower())
            else "other"
            for row in self.rows
        )
        return f"of_ {forms['of_']}, bare {forms['bare']}, other {forms['other']}"

    def by_canonical(self) -> dict[str, Listed]:
        return {row.canonical_id: row for row in self.rows}


def _listing(client: PlaudClient) -> Listing:
    """Every page until an empty one, never stopping at a short one (§11.2)."""
    rows: list[Listed] = []
    malformed = 0
    for page in range(1, PAGE_CAP + 1):
        result = client.list_page(page)
        if not result.rows and not result.malformed:
            return Listing(rows, malformed, page)
        rows += result.rows
        malformed += result.malformed
    raise SpikeRefused(f"stopped: the listing reached {PAGE_CAP} pages, which makes it bad")


def _raw_rows(client: PlaudClient) -> list[dict]:
    """Every listed row as Plaud gave it (S9's listing fields, S12's times), paging alike."""
    rows: list[dict] = []
    for page in range(1, PAGE_CAP + 1):
        _shape, batch = _batch(client.get_json(f"{LIST_PATH}?page={page}&page_size={PAGE_SIZE}"))
        if not batch:
            return rows
        rows += [row for row in batch if isinstance(row, dict)]
    raise SpikeRefused(f"stopped: the listing reached {PAGE_CAP} pages, which makes it bad")


def _files(client: PlaudClient, listed_id: str) -> dict:
    """files/{id}, without fetching the blocks behind links (S7, S9, S11)."""
    env = client.get_json(FILE_PATH.format(urllib.parse.quote(listed_id, safe="")))
    if not isinstance(env, dict):
        raise SpikeRefused("stopped: files/{id} didn't answer an object")
    return env


def _resolve(session: Session, given: str) -> str:
    """--id is a Plaud ID, in any form, or an archive recording ID: then its first Plaud ID."""
    if ID_RE.fullmatch(given):
        try:
            ids = _plaud_ids(session.archive.load(given))
        except (KeyError, ValueError):
            ids = []
        if not ids:
            raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: {short(given)} is no recording with a Plaud source")
        return ids[0]
    return canonical_plaud_id(given)


def _named(session: Session, listing: Listing, count: int) -> list[Listed]:
    """The recordings Dan named with --id, as listed, each passed by the guard."""
    if not session.args.id:
        raise SpikeRefused(f"refused: name up to {count} recordings with --id")
    found = listing.by_canonical()
    allowed = []
    for given in session.args.id[:count]:
        canonical = _resolve(session, given)
        row = found.get(canonical)
        if row is None:
            say(f"{short(canonical)}: not listed")
        elif session.guard.allows(row.listed_id, row.title, own_clip=session.args.own_clip):
            allowed.append(row)
        else:
            say(f"{short(canonical)}: refused by the guard")
    return allowed


class _NoRedirect(urllib.request.HTTPRedirectHandler):
    def redirect_request(self, req, fp, code, msg, headers, newurl):
        return None


def _post_form(url: str, fields: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int | None, dict]:
    """One form POST to the token URL, never redirected: the status and the reply's JSON object,
    or (None, {}) when unreachable. Nothing of it is printed here."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        url,
        data=urllib.parse.urlencode(fields).encode("ascii"),
        method="POST",
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "Accept": "application/json"},
    )
    try:
        with urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect).open(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            status, body = response.status, response.read()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        status, body = exc.code, exc.read()
        exc.close()
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError):
        return None, {}
    try:
        reply = json.loads(body)
    except ValueError:
        reply = {}
    return status, reply if isinstance(reply, dict) else {}


def _raw_get(url: str, headers: dict[str, str]) -> tuple[int | None, list[str]]:
    """A GET that reads at most one byte, never redirected: the status and the header names."""
    request = urllib.request.Request(url, method="GET", headers=headers)
    try:
        with urllib.request.build_opener(_NoRedirect).open(request, timeout=TIMEOUT) as response:
            response.read(1)
            return response.status, list(response.headers.keys())
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
        names = list(exc.headers.keys())
        exc.close()
        return exc.code, names
    except (urllib.error.URLError, OSError, ValueError):
        return None, []


def _token_url(url: str | None) -> str:
    parts = urllib.parse.urlsplit(url) if isinstance(url, str) else None
    if parts is None or parts.scheme != "https" or not parts.hostname:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: --token-url must be the https token URL session A's S1 found")
    return url


def _save_tokens(session: Session, data: dict, reply: dict) -> None:
    """Keep the session's sign-in usable after a refresh: the reply's tokens replace the old ones
    in the token file, written atomically at 0600 in the spike folder."""
    new = dict(data)
    for key in ("access_token", "refresh_token", "expires_in", "expires_at", "token_type"):
        if key in reply:
            new[key] = reply[key]
    path = session.tokens.path
    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=path.parent, prefix=".tokens-")  # created at 0600
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            json.dump(new, fh)
            fh.flush()
            os.fsync(fh.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp, path)
    except BaseException:
        Path(tmp).unlink(missing_ok=True)
        raise


def _claims(token: object) -> dict | None:
    """A JWT's claims, for their names and times only; None for anything else."""
    if not isinstance(token, str) or token.count(".") != 2:
        return None
    middle = token.split(".")[1]
    try:
        claims = json.loads(base64.urlsafe_b64decode(middle + "=" * (-len(middle) % 4)))
    except ValueError:
        return None
    return claims if isinstance(claims, dict) else None


# -- the spikes ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def s1(session: Session) -> None:
    """The token's shape and lifetime: key names, token type, expiries, a refresh token."""
    try:
        data = session.tokens.data()
    except PlaudAuthError:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: no readable token file at --token-file") from None
    say(f"token file keys: {_names(data)}")
    kind = data.get("token_type")
    say(f"token type: {kind if isinstance(kind, str) and kind.isalpha() else 'unknown'}")
    say(f"refresh token: {_yes(data.get('refresh_token'))}")
    for key in sorted(data):
        if "expire" in key.lower() or key.lower() in ("exp", "iat", "obtained_at", "created_at"):
            say(f"{key}: {_time(data[key])}")
    for name in ("access_token", "refresh_token"):
        claims = _claims(data.get(name))
        if claims is None:
            say(f"{name}: not a JWT")
            continue
        say(f"{name} claims: {_names(claims)}")
        if isinstance(claims.get("exp"), int | float):
            say(f"{name} expires: {_time(claims['exp'])}")
        if all(isinstance(claims.get(k), int | float) for k in ("exp", "iat")):
            say(f"{name} lifetime: {int(claims['exp'] - claims['iat']) // 60} min")


def s2(session: Session) -> None:
    """Refresh and rotation: one refresh, the old refresh token again, then one listing page."""
    url = _token_url(session.args.token_url)
    data = session.tokens.data()
    old = data.get("refresh_token")
    if not isinstance(old, str) or not old:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: the sign-in has no refresh token: stop and ask Dan (S1)")
    status, reply = _post_form(url, {"grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": old})
    say(f"refresh: HTTP {status}{_code(reply)}")
    if status != 200 or not reply.get("access_token"):
        say("the refresh was refused from this machine: stop and ask Dan")
        return
    new = reply.get("refresh_token")
    say(f"reply keys: {_names(reply)}")
    say(f"new refresh token: {_yes(new)} · rotated: {_yes(new and new != old)}")
    if "expires_in" in reply:
        say(f"expires_in: {_time(reply['expires_in'])}")
    _save_tokens(session, data, reply)
    again, again_reply = _post_form(url, {"grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": old})
    say(f"the old refresh token again: HTTP {again}{_code(again_reply)}")
    if again == 200 and again_reply.get("access_token"):
        _save_tokens(session, session.tokens.data(), again_reply)  # the newest pair is kept
    try:
        page = session.client.list_page(1, 10)
        say(f"one listing page with the new access token: ok, {len(page.rows)} rows")
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"one listing page with the new access token: {_error(exc)}")


def s3(session: Session) -> None:
    """Does a second sign-in sign the first out? One cheap call with the session's sign-in."""
    try:
        session.client.list_page(1, 10)
        say("signed in: yes")
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"signed in: no ({_error(exc)})")


def s4(session: Session) -> None:
    """A refused refresh: a copy of the refresh token with one character changed."""
    url = _token_url(session.args.token_url)
    old = session.tokens.data().get("refresh_token")
    if not isinstance(old, str) or not old:
        raise SpikeRefused("refused: the sign-in has no refresh token: stop and ask Dan (S1)")
    changed = old[:-1] + ("A" if old[-1] != "A" else "B")
    status, reply = _post_form(url, {"grant_type": "refresh_token", "refresh_token": changed})
    say(f"refused refresh: HTTP {status}{_code(reply)}")


def _pass(client: PlaudClient, n: int) -> set[str]:
    listing = _listing(client)
    ids = [row.canonical_id for row in listing.rows]
    unique = set(ids)
    say(
        f"pass {n}: {len(unique)} IDs, {len(ids) - len(unique)} repeats, {listing.malformed} "
        f"malformed, {listing.pages} pages · census {listing.census()} · "
        f"ID set {short(','.join(sorted(unique)))}"
    )
    return unique


def s5(session: Session) -> None:
    """The listing's shape, a cheap change signal, and paging."""
    for size in SIZES:
        try:
            payload = session.client.get_json(f"{LIST_PATH}?page=1&page_size={size}")
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"page 1 at size {size}: {_error(exc)}")
            continue
        shape, batch = _batch(payload)
        rows = [row for row in batch if isinstance(row, dict)]
        say(f"page 1 at size {size}: {len(batch)} rows, {shape}")
        say(f"  row fields: {_names({key for row in rows for key in row})}")
        for key, value in sorted(payload.items() if isinstance(payload, dict) else []):
            if isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool):
                say(f"  {key}: {value}")
    first = _pass(session.client, 1)
    sleep(PAUSE)
    second = _pass(session.client, 2)
    say(
        f"same ID set: {_yes(first == second)} · only in pass 1: {len(first - second)} · "
        f"only in pass 2: {len(second - first)}"
    )


def s7(session: Session) -> None:
    """The ID form: listing IDs against the archive's, the consent list, and three audio hashes.
    The archive is read itself, because the index lives in a Docker volume."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    listed = set(listing.by_canonical())
    here = {
        pid: rec.media.sha256
        for rec in session.archive.iter_recordings()
        for pid in _plaud_ids(rec)
    }
    say(f"listed: {len(listed)} · census {listing.census()}")
    say(
        f"in the archive: {len(listed & set(here))} · listed, not in the archive: "
        f"{len(listed - set(here))} · in the archive, not listed: {len(set(here) - listed)}"
    )
    say(f"consent-list IDs in the listing: {len(session.guard.consent & listed)}")
    named = _named(session, listing, 3)
    for row in named:
        name = short(row.canonical_id)
        if row.canonical_id not in here:
            say(f"{name}: not in the archive")
            continue
        dest = session.folder / f"s7-{name}.audio"
        try:
            env = _files(session.client, row.listed_id)
            link = check_link(env.get("presigned_url"), api_base=session.client.api_base)
            session.client.download(link, dest)
            say(f"{name}: audio identical: {_yes(sha256_file(dest) == here[row.canonical_id])}")
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"{name}: {_error(exc)}")
        finally:
            dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)
    if named:
        bare = named[0].canonical_id
        for label, form in (("of_ form", f"of_{bare}"), ("bare hex", bare)):
            try:
                _files(session.client, form)
                say(f"files/{{id}} by its {label}: ok")
            except PlaudError as exc:
                say(f"files/{{id}} by its {label}: {_error(exc)}")


def _blocks(env: dict) -> list[dict]:
    blocks = []
    for section in ("source_list", "note_list"):
        value = env.get(section)
        blocks += [b for b in value if isinstance(b, dict)] if isinstance(value, list) else []
    return blocks


def s8(session: Session) -> None:
    """The envelope and volatility: five recordings, each fetched twice, a minute apart."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    owners: dict[str, set[str]] = collections.defaultdict(set)  # embeddingKey's hash -> recordings
    for row in _named(session, listing, 5):
        name = short(row.canonical_id)
        try:
            first = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
            sleep(PAUSE)
            second = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"{name}: {_error(exc)}")
            continue
        say(f"{name}: envelope keys: {_names(first)}")
        say(f"{name}: audio link expires in {_expires(first.get('presigned_url'))}")
        for block in _blocks(first):
            kind = block.get("data_type")
            kind = kind if isinstance(kind, str) and kind.isidentifier() else "unknown"
            link, error = block.get("data_link"), block.get("_data_link_error")
            line = f"{name}: block {kind}: keys {_names(block)} · behind a link: {_yes(link)}"
            if link:
                line += f" · link expires in {_expires(link)}"
            if isinstance(error, str) and error.isidentifier():
                line += f" · error {error}"
            say(line)
        rows = transcript_rows(first) or []
        say(f"{name}: segments: {len(rows)}")
        for r in rows:
            if isinstance(r.get("embeddingKey"), str) and r["embeddingKey"]:
                owners[short(r["embeddingKey"])].add(row.canonical_id)
        before, after = part_hashes(first), part_hashes(second)
        for part in sorted(set(before) | set(after)):
            label = "notes" if part.startswith("notes:") else part  # a tab's name is Dan's
            say(f"{name}: part {label}: matched {_yes(before.get(part) == after.get(part))}")
    shared = sum(1 for recordings in owners.values() if len(recordings) > 1)
    say(f"embeddingKey values seen in more than one recording: {shared}")


def _changed(new: dict, old: dict) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(k for k in set(new) | set(old) if new.get(k) != old.get(k))


def s9(session: Session) -> None:
    """What an edit looks like, on Dan's own throwaway clip (session C). Without --id: the newest
    listed rows, for (a). With --id (and --own-clip): the clip's parts and listing fields, and what
    changed since the last run."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    if not session.args.id:
        dated = [row for row in listing.rows if row.recorded_at]
        for row in sorted(dated, key=lambda r: r.recorded_at, reverse=True)[:5]:
            minutes = int((session.now() - row.recorded_at).total_seconds() // 60)
            word = keep_out_match(row.title, session.guard.words) is not None
            say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: keep-out word: {_yes(word)} · {minutes} min old")
        return
    canonical = _resolve(session, session.args.id[0])
    name = short(canonical)
    record_path = session.folder / "s9-last.json"
    try:
        last = json.loads(record_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        last = {}
    row = listing.by_canonical().get(canonical)
    say(f"{name}: listed: {_yes(row)}")
    if row is None:
        # Its title was checked by the run that recorded it; consent and private are checked now.
        checked = last.get("id") == name and last.get("pattern_ok") is True
        if not checked or not session.guard.allows(canonical, "", own_clip=True):
            say(f"{name}: files/{{id}} not fetched: no earlier run checked its title")
            return
        try:
            _files(session.client, session.args.id[0])
            say(f"{name}: files/{{id}}: ok")
        except PlaudError as exc:
            say(f"{name}: files/{{id}}: {_error(exc)}")
        return
    say(f"{name}: keep-out word: {_yes(keep_out_match(row.title, session.guard.words))}")
    if not session.guard.allows(row.listed_id, row.title, own_clip=session.args.own_clip):
        say(f"{name}: refused by the guard")
        return
    raw = next(
        (r for r in _raw_rows(session.client) if canonical_plaud_id(str(r.get("id"))) == canonical),
        {},
    )
    try:
        first = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
        sleep(MOMENT)
        second = session.client.envelope(row.listed_id)
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"{name}: {_error(exc)}")
        return
    parts = {p: h[:8] for p, h in part_hashes(first).items()}
    again = {p: h[:8] for p, h in part_hashes(second).items()}
    say(f"{name}: parts that differ a moment apart: {_names(_changed(parts, again))}")
    fields = {key: short(json.dumps(value, sort_keys=True)) for key, value in raw.items()}
    record = {
        "id": name,
        "at": session.now().isoformat(),
        "parts": parts,
        "fields": fields,
        "pattern_ok": True,
    }
    if last.get("id") == name:
        seconds = int((session.now() - datetime.fromisoformat(last["at"])).total_seconds())
        say(f"{name}: parts changed since the last run: {_names(_changed(parts, last['parts']))}")
        changed_fields = _names(_changed(fields, last["fields"]))
        say(f"{name}: listing fields changed since the last run: {changed_fields}")
        say(f"{name}: seconds since the last run: {seconds}")
    record_path.write_text(json.dumps(record), encoding="utf-8")
    record_path.chmod(0o600)


def s10(session: Session) -> None:
    """Pacing: twenty calls at one a second, and the rate-limit headers' names. It stops at the
    first 429: a spike never provokes one on purpose."""
    url = f"{session.client.api_base}{LIST_PATH}?page=1&page_size=10"
    limits: set[str] = set()
    statuses: collections.Counter[str] = collections.Counter()
    for n in range(20):
        auth = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {session.tokens.access_token()}"}
        status, names = _raw_get(url, {**auth, "User-Agent": "recordings-spike"})
        statuses[str(status)] += 1
        limits |= {h for h in names if "ratelimit" in h.lower() or "retry" in h.lower()}
        if status == 429:
            say(f"stopped at call {n + 1}: HTTP 429")
            break
        sleep(1.0)
    say(f"statuses: {', '.join(f'{k} ×{v}' for k, v in sorted(statuses.items()))}")
    retry_after = any(h.lower() == "retry-after" for h in limits)
    say(f"rate-limit headers: {_names(limits)} · Retry-After seen: {_yes(retry_after)}")


def s11(session: Session) -> None:
    """A large download: size, time, throughput, Content-Length, Range, and the link's expiry."""
    named = _named(session, _listing(session.client), 1)
    if not named:
        return
    row = named[0]
    try:
        env = _files(session.client, row.listed_id)
        link = check_link(env.get("presigned_url"), api_base=session.client.api_base)
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: {_error(exc)}")
        return
    status, _names_seen = _raw_get(link, {"Range": "bytes=0-0"})
    say(f"Range honoured: {_yes(status == 206)} (HTTP {status})")
    dest = session.folder / "s11.audio"
    start = session.monotonic()
    try:
        size = session.client.download(link, dest)
        seconds = max(session.monotonic() - start, 0.001)
        say(f"size: {size / 1e6:.1f} MB · {seconds:.0f} s · {size / 1e6 / seconds:.2f} MB/s")
        say("Content-Length: present")  # download() refuses a body without one
        expires = _expires(link)
        passed = expires != "unknown" and seconds > float(expires.split()[0])
        say(f"link expires in {expires} · its expiry passed during the download: {_yes(passed)}")
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"download: {_error(exc)}")
    finally:
        dest.unlink(missing_ok=True)


def s12(session: Session) -> None:
    """Time zones: Plaud's start time for three recordings Dan remembers, read both ways."""
    listing = _listing(session.client)
    raw = {canonical_plaud_id(str(r.get("id"))): r for r in _raw_rows(session.client)}
    zone = ZoneInfo(session.cfg.default_timezone)
    for row in _named(session, listing, 3):
        given = raw.get(row.canonical_id, {}).get("start_at")
        if not isinstance(given, str) or row.start_at is None:
            say(f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: no start time")
            continue
        marked = "Z" if given.endswith("Z") else "an offset, or nothing"
        as_utc = row.start_at.astimezone(zone).strftime("%H:%M")
        as_local = row.start_at.replace(tzinfo=None).strftime("%H:%M")
        say(
            f"{short(row.canonical_id)}: marked {marked} · read as UTC, in "
            f"{session.cfg.default_timezone}: {as_utc} · read as local time: {as_local}"
        )


SPIKE_FUNCTIONS: dict[str, Callable[[Session], None]] = {
    "s1": s1,
    "s2": s2,
    "s3": s3,
    "s4": s4,
    "s5": s5,
    "s7": s7,
    "s8": s8,
    "s9": s9,
    "s10": s10,
    "s11": s11,
    "s12": s12,
}


def _parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="plaud_spike.py", description="stage 2b's spikes (§18)")
    ap.add_argument("spike", choices=SPIKES)
    ap.add_argument(
        "--home",
        default=os.environ.get("RECORDINGS_HOME"),
        help="RECORDINGS_HOME, the spike folder's parent",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--token-file", type=Path, help="the session's token file, in the spike folder")
    ap.add_argument(
        "--id",
        action="append",
        default=[],
        help="a Plaud ID or an archive recording ID (S7, S8, S9, S11, S12)",
    )
    ap.add_argument("--token-url", help="the https token URL session A's S1 found (S2, S4)")
    ap.add_argument("--own-clip", action="store_true", help="S9 only: skip the keep-out check")
    return ap


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    args = _parser().parse_args(argv)
    guard: Guard | None = None
    try:
        if args.own_clip and args.spike != "s9":
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: --own-clip is for S9 only")
        if args.spike in ("s2", "s4"):
            _token_url(args.token_url)  # before anything is read
        elif args.token_url is not None:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: --token-url is for S2 and S4 only")
        if not args.home:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: give --home (RECORDINGS_HOME)")
        cfg = load_config(os.environ)
        if cfg.archive_path is None:
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: no archive is configured, so private ones can't be known")
        archive = Archive(cfg.archive_path)
        guard = build_guard(cfg, archive)
        folder = spike_folder(Path(args.home))
        token_file = (args.token_file or folder / "home" / ".plaud" / "tokens.json").absolute()
        if not token_file.resolve().is_relative_to(folder.resolve()):
            raise SpikeRefused("refused: --token-file must be inside the spike folder")
        tokens = FileTokens(token_file)
        api_base = check_api_base(_section(cfg, "plaud").get("api_base", API_BASE))
        client = PlaudClient(tokens, api_base=api_base)
        SPIKE_FUNCTIONS[args.spike](Session(args, cfg, archive, guard, folder, tokens, client))
        return 0
    except SpikeRefused as exc:
        say(str(exc))
        return EXIT_REFUSED
    except ConfigError as exc:
        say(f"refused: {exc}")
        return EXIT_REFUSED
    except PlaudError as exc:
        say(f"stopped: {_error(exc)}")
        return 1
    finally:
        if guard is not None:
            say(guard.report())


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())
```

```text
### 1c. Before stage 2b (not needed for 2a)

The token spike and the ID-form spike (§9.1, §19) both call Plaud. Stage 2a makes no Plaud
calls, so they run before stage 2b's deploy, not now.
```

````text
### 1c. Before stage 2b (not needed for 2a)

Stage 2b's spikes (its spec's §18) are the first steps that call Plaud, so none of them runs for
2a. Each is a supervised session with Dan, run with `scripts/plaud_spike.py`, before the stage 2b
work that needs its result: **A**, the sign-in (s1, s2, s4, s3; about 45 minutes); **B**, the data
(s5, s7, s8, s10, s12, s11; about an hour); **C**, an edit on a throwaway clip (s9; about 45
minutes). Read the script before each session. It prints only counts, yes or no, times, status
codes, field names and 8-hex hashes: never a token, a title, transcript text or a whole Plaud ID.
Before any call it reads the consent list fail-closed, and it refuses any consent-listed or
private recording, and any title the keep-out word or a private pattern matches; it ends by
saying how many it refused.

**On the homelab server,** in `$REPO_DIR`, with uv installed for your user (see uv's own
installation page, https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/):
```bash

install -d -m 700 "$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike"
${EDITOR:-vi} "$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike/config.toml"
export RECORDINGS_CONFIG="$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike/config.toml"
```
The session's own config uses this server's paths, because the containers' `/archive`, `/state`
and `/consent` don't exist out here: `[archive] path` and `default_timezone`, `[state] path`,
`[plaud] consent_list` (the list's path on this server), and `[plaud] auto_private_patterns` and
`keep_out_word`, copied from `config.toml` if they are set there. It holds no secret.

**The session's sign-in,** on the Mac, under a temporary `HOME`, so the Mac's own Plaud sign-ins
are untouched. The token file goes into the spike folder without being printed. `HOMELAB` and
`SRV_HOME` are as section 3 sets them.
```bash
tmphome="$(mktemp -d)" && chmod 700 "$tmphome"
HOME="$tmphome" plaud login
ssh "$HOMELAB" "umask 077 && mkdir -p '$SRV_HOME/spike/home/.plaud' && cat > '$SRV_HOME/spike/home/.plaud/tokens.json'" < "$tmphome/.plaud/tokens.json"
rm -rf "$tmphome"
```

**Each spike,** on the homelab server, in that shell: `uv run python scripts/plaud_spike.py s1`,
and so on. S2 and S4 also take `--token-url` (the https token URL S1 finds), and S7, S8, S9, S11
and S12 take one `--id` per recording Dan names (a Plaud ID or an archive recording ID). S9 takes
`--own-clip` for Dan's throwaway clip. Exit 78 means the guard refused before any call; it says
why.

**At the end of each session,** delete the spike folder, the session's sign-in with it:
```bash
rm -rf "$RECORDINGS_HOME/spike"
```

**Results.** After each session, fill in its date and each outcome. Never a recording's date,
time or duration, a token, a title or an ID.

| Spike | Session, date | Outcome |
|---|---|---|
| S1 the token's shape and lifetime | A, | |
| S2 refresh and rotation | A, | |
| S4 a refused refresh | A, | |
| S3 a second sign-in elsewhere | A, | |
| S5 the listing's shape and paging | B, | |
| S7 the ID form | B, | |
| S8 the envelope and volatility | B, | |
| S10 pacing | B, | |
| S12 time zones | B, | |
| S11 a large download | B, | |
| S9 what an edit looks like | C, | |
````

  ```sql
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_requests (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, request_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    plaud_ids TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', recording_ids TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    select_all INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    state TEXT NOT NULL,                     -- queued | running | done | failed | expired
    queued_at TEXT NOT NULL, started_at TEXT, finished_at TEXT,
    progress TEXT,                           -- JSON {"done", "total"}
    message TEXT,                            -- a §15.6 reply phrase
    result TEXT);                            -- JSON: counts and IDs, never a title
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_requests_by_state ON plaud_requests (state, id);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_listing (
    canonical_plaud_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, listed_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    first_seen TEXT NOT NULL, last_seen TEXT NOT NULL, absent_since TEXT,
    kept_out_at TEXT, kept_out_word TEXT,    -- by a word (§12.2); a late keep-out's too
    rekey_of TEXT,                           -- §11.4 step 6: the absent ID it matched, or '*' for several
    released_at TEXT,                        -- §12.2
    needs_review INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, -- §11.6
    import_failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, next_import_at TEXT, parked_at TEXT,
    title_sha256 TEXT, duration_ms INTEGER, change_marker TEXT);   -- only while its recording is here
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_checks (
    recording_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, last_checked_at TEXT, last_changed_at TEXT, next_check_at TEXT,
    interval_seconds INTEGER, fast_checks_left INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    failures INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, failing_since TEXT,
    settled INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, baseline_pending INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    held_removals TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', parked_at TEXT, degraded INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    gone_since TEXT, kept_here_at TEXT);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_check_log (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, at TEXT NOT NULL, recording_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    result TEXT NOT NULL, parts_changed TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]',
    parts_volatile TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]', counted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, failure_class TEXT);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_check_log_by_at ON plaud_check_log (at);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_private_checked (
    recording_id TEXT NOT NULL, canonical_plaud_id TEXT NOT NULL, title_sha256 TEXT NOT NULL,
    patterns_version INTEGER NOT NULL, checked_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (recording_id, canonical_plaud_id));
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, at TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL,
    recording_id TEXT, canonical_plaud_id TEXT,
    detail TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',       -- JSON: parts, a fixed "why"; never a title
    open INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, resolved_at TEXT);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events_by_at ON plaud_events (at);
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events_one_flag ON plaud_events (recording_id)
    WHERE open = 1 AND kind IN ('kept-out-late', 'consent-late');
  CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS plaud_events_one_unwritten ON plaud_events (recording_id)
    WHERE open = 1 AND kind = 'private-unwritten';
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plaud_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  ```
- Produces (`recordings/plaud/checks.py`):
  ```python
  NO_SYNC_YET = "No sync has run yet"
  class NoSyncYet(Exception): ...
  def no_such_table(exc: BaseException) -> bool: ...   # sqlite3.OperationalError "no such table"
  EVENT_KINDS = ("imported", "arrived-private", "updated", "retagged-private", "kept-out-late",
                 "consent-late", "private-unwritten", "kept-here", "gone", "released", "rekeyed")
  FLAG_KINDS = ("kept-out-late", "consent-late")
  BLOCKERS = ("sign-in", "consent", "hold", "breaker", "private-unwritten")
  BLOCKER_PREFIX = "blocker:"
  # plaud_state keys (decision 17)
  K_LAST_GOOD_LISTING = "last_good_listing"; K_HOLD = "hold"; K_BREAKER = "breaker"; K_SIGN_IN = "sign_in"
  K_FAILING = "failing"; K_LAST_PING = "last_ping"; K_LAST_STARTED = "last_started"; K_LAST_ENDED = "last_ended"
  K_LAST_TURN = "last_turn"; K_CATCH_UP_DONE = "catch_up_done_at"; K_SNAPSHOT_MARK = "snapshot_mark"
  K_REBUILT = "rebuilt_at"; K_KEEP_OUT_WORDS = "keep_out_words"; K_PATTERNS = "patterns"
  K_PATTERNS_PASS = "patterns_pass"; K_CONSENT = "consent"; K_FULL = "full_sync"; K_RETIRED = "retired_at"
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class Marker:
      canonical_plaud_id: str
      title_sha256: str
      patterns_version: int
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class ListingRow: ...   # one field per plaud_listing column, same names
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class CheckRow: ...     # one field per plaud_checks column, same names
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class Event:
      id: int; at: datetime; kind: str; recording_id: str | None; canonical_plaud_id: str | None
      detail: dict; open: bool; resolved_at: datetime | None
  class PlaudDB:
      def __init__(self, state: State) -> None: ...
      # plaud_state (values are JSON)
      def get(self, key: str) -> Any | None: ...
      def put(self, key: str, value: Any, *, now: datetime) -> None: ...
      def put_many(self, values: Mapping[str, Any], *, now: datetime) -> None: ...   # one transaction
      def delete(self, key: str) -> None: ...
      def with_prefix(self, prefix: str) -> dict[str, Any]: ...
      # plaud_listing, by any form of the ID
      def listing(self, plaud_id: str) -> ListingRow | None: ...
      def upsert_listed(self, listed_id: str, *, now: datetime) -> ListingRow: ...   # first sight sets first_seen; listed_id follows the newest form
      def set_listing(self, plaud_id: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...   # plaud_listing column names only (ValueError otherwise)
      # plaud_checks
      def check_row(self, recording_id: str) -> CheckRow | None: ...
      def set_check(self, recording_id: str, **fields: Any) -> None: ...
      # plaud_events
      def add_event(self, kind: str, *, now: datetime, recording_id: str | None = None, plaud_id: str | None = None,
                    detail: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, open_flag: bool = False) -> int: ...
      def open_flags(self, kinds: Iterable[str] = FLAG_KINDS) -> list[Event]: ...
      def resolve(self, event_id: int, *, now: datetime) -> None: ...
      def change_kind(self, event_id: int, kind: str) -> None: ...
      def events_since(self, since: datetime, kinds: Iterable[str]) -> list[Event]: ...
      # plaud_private_checked
      def markers(self, recording_id: str) -> dict[str, Marker]: ...
      def set_markers(self, recording_id: str, markers: Iterable[Marker], *, now: datetime) -> None: ...
      def prune(self, *, now: datetime) -> None: ...   # check log 7 days; events 90 days, open flags kept
  ```
  Every reader raises `NoSyncYet` instead of `sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table`.
- Produces (`recordings/plaud/cache.py`), a separate SQLite file Phase 2 writes:
  ```python
  CACHE_NAME = "plaud-cache.db"
  PREVIEW_LIFE = timedelta(minutes=10)
  CACHE_SCHEMA = """
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS compare_rows (
    canonical_plaud_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, listed_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    bucket TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- waiting | missing | excluded
    reason TEXT NOT NULL,                 -- a §15.1 state phrase
    start_at TEXT, duration_ms INTEGER,
    title TEXT,                           -- waiting or missing only; never kept out, consent-listed or under review
    arrives_private INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, review INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, excluded_by TEXT);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS keyed_out (     -- consent-listed and kept-out IDs, for §11.4 step 6
    canonical_plaud_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, kind TEXT NOT NULL, start_at TEXT, duration_ms INTEGER,
    last_listed_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS release_preview (
    canonical_plaud_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, request_id TEXT NOT NULL, title TEXT NOT NULL, created_at TEXT NOT NULL);
  CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT NOT NULL);   -- "compare": the equations and titles_hidden, JSON
  """
  @dataclass(frozen=True)
  class CompareRow: ...   # one field per compare_rows column
  class Cache:
      def __init__(self, state_dir: Path) -> None: ...      # <state_dir>/plaud-cache.db
      @classmethod
      def read_only(cls, state_dir: Path) -> Cache | None: ...   # None when the file isn't there
      def db(self) -> AbstractContextManager[sqlite3.Connection]: ...   # creates the file and schema on first write
      def compare_rows(self) -> list[CompareRow]: ...
      def summary(self) -> dict | None: ...                 # meta "compare", decoded
      def release_title(self, plaud_id: str, *, now: datetime) -> str | None: ...   # None once older than PREVIEW_LIFE
      def drop_preview(self, plaud_id: str) -> None: ...
  ```
- `Index`: every connection that creates or rebuilds sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`.
- `State.forget(file)`: also deletes the recording's `plaud_checks`, `plaud_private_checked` and `plaud_events` rows, and clears `title_sha256`, `duration_ms` and `change_marker` on the `plaud_listing` rows of its canonical IDs (read from `plaud_private_checked` before deleting).
