  - `scripts/consent_id.py <text>`: prints the one ID found in `<text>` (a bare ID, `of_…`, or the Copy ID form `` - `of_…` — ``) exactly as typed, or exits 1 with "not a Plaud ID".
  - `docker/consent-add.sh <id>` (POSIX `sh`, on the server): refuses an ID not matching `^(of_)?[0-9a-fA-F]{32}$`; reads `RECORDINGS_CONSENT_HOST` from `docker/deploy.env`; writes the old list plus `` - `<id>` — added <YYYY-MM-DD> `` to a temporary file in the same folder at the old file's mode, then renames it over.
  - `make consent-add ID=<id>`: `SERVER` and `REPO_DIR` from `local.mk` (git-ignored, `-include`d, expanded on the Mac); runs `scripts/consent_id.py`, then `ssh "$(SERVER)" "cd '$(REPO_DIR)' && sh docker/consent-add.sh '<id>' && sh docker/up-deployed.sh exec -T worker recordings plaud consent"`; non-zero on any failure, naming the step.
  Two precisions. `consent_id.py` prints the hex exactly as typed, after a lower-case `of_` when the ID had one in any case: `consent-add.sh`'s pattern takes `of_` only, while the list's grammar reads `OF_` too. `ops-busy.py` with no lock name exits 2 (usage). A new list (none there yet) is made at mode 0600.

```python
"""Make targets that reach the server (stage 2b spec §21's shell targets), run for real against a
fake `ssh` on PATH: the remote command runs in a temporary folder that stands for the server's
checkout, with the real docker/consent-add.sh. Synthetic IDs only; nothing leaves the machine."""

import os
import re
import shutil
import stat
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from types import SimpleNamespace

import pytest

REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]
PLAUD_A = "of_" + f"{1:032x}"  # synthetic Plaud IDs
PLAUD_B = f"{2:032X}"  # bare, upper case
ADDED = r"added \d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}"


@pytest.fixture
def server(tmp_path):
    """The stand-in: a checkout with docker/consent-add.sh, a deploy.env naming a consent folder,
    an up-deployed.sh that only records its arguments, and an ssh that logs the host and the
    command, then runs the command there."""
    if shutil.which("make") is None:
        pytest.skip("make is not installed")
    checkout = tmp_path / "server" / "repo"
    (checkout / "docker").mkdir(parents=True)
    shutil.copy2(REPO / "docker" / "consent-add.sh", checkout / "docker" / "consent-add.sh")
    consent = tmp_path / "server" / "consent"
    consent.mkdir(mode=0o700)
    (checkout / "docker" / "deploy.env").write_text(
        f"RECORDINGS_CONSENT_HOST={consent}\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    log = tmp_path / "ssh.log"
    (checkout / "docker" / "up-deployed.sh").write_text(
        f'printf "up-deployed %s\\n" "$*" >> "{log}"\n', encoding="utf-8"
    )
    bin_dir = tmp_path / "bin"
    bin_dir.mkdir()
    (bin_dir / "ssh").write_text(
        "#!/bin/sh\n"
        f'printf "host %s\\n" "$1" >> "{log}"\n'
        "shift\n"
        f'printf "command %s\\n" "$*" >> "{log}"\n'
        'exec sh -c "$*"\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    (bin_dir / "ssh").chmod(0o755)
    env = {**os.environ, "PATH": f"{bin_dir}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    return SimpleNamespace(checkout=checkout, list=consent / "consent-list.md", log=log, env=env)


def consent_add(server, value: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    return subprocess.run(
        [
            "make",
            "--no-print-directory",
            "consent-add",
            f"ID={value}",
            "SERVER=homelab-test",
            f"REPO_DIR={server.checkout}",
        ],
        cwd=REPO,
        env=server.env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )


def test_consent_add_refuses_a_bad_id_before_ssh(server):
    for bad in ("not-an-id", "0" * 31, "of_" + "0" * 33, "- `" + "g" * 32 + "` —", "x\n" + PLAUD_A):
        done = consent_add(server, bad)
        assert done.returncode != 0 and "not a Plaud ID" in done.stderr, bad
    assert not server.log.exists()  # ssh never ran
    assert not server.list.exists()
    # the server's own check refuses too, before the list is touched
    direct = subprocess.run(
        ["sh", "docker/consent-add.sh", f"{PLAUD_A}; touch hacked"],
        cwd=server.checkout,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    assert direct.returncode == 2 and "not a Plaud ID" in direct.stderr
    assert not server.list.exists() and not (server.checkout / "hacked").exists()


def test_consent_add_writes_by_rename_and_keeps_the_mode(server):
    # why: the worker watches the folder; a list written in place could be read half-written.
    kept = f"{9:032x}"
    server.list.write_text(f"# Consent list (synthetic)\n- `{kept}` — asked", encoding="utf-8")
    server.list.chmod(0o400)  # the runbook makes it read-only
    before = server.list.stat().st_ino
    done = consent_add(server, PLAUD_A)
    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr
    after = server.list.stat()
    assert after.st_ino != before  # a new file, renamed over the old one
    assert stat.S_IMODE(after.st_mode) == 0o400
    lines = server.list.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    assert lines[:2] == ["# Consent list (synthetic)", f"- `{kept}` — asked"]
    assert re.fullmatch(rf"- `{PLAUD_A}` — {ADDED}", lines[2]) and len(lines) == 3
    assert [p.name for p in server.list.parent.iterdir()] == ["consent-list.md"]  # no temp left
    assert "up-deployed exec -T worker recordings plaud consent" in server.log.read_text()


def test_consent_add_accepts_the_copy_id_form(server):
    # Review Focus 4: the Sync screen's Copy ID copies the list's own form; pasted into
    # `make consent-add ID=…`, it adds the ID, never a typo line that stops every import.
    done = consent_add(server, f"- `{PLAUD_A}` —")
    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr
    assert re.fullmatch(rf"- `{PLAUD_A}` — {ADDED}\n", server.list.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert stat.S_IMODE(server.list.stat().st_mode) == 0o600  # a new list
    assert consent_add(server, PLAUD_B).returncode == 0  # bare and upper case, as typed
    assert consent_add(server, f"OF_{3:032x}").returncode == 0  # the prefix in any case
    lines = server.list.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
    assert re.fullmatch(rf"- `{PLAUD_B}` — {ADDED}", lines[1])
    assert re.fullmatch(rf"- `of_{3:032x}` — {ADDED}", lines[2])


def test_consent_add_expands_server_and_repo_dir_on_the_mac(server, tmp_path):
    # why: the server's shell has no SERVER or REPO_DIR. make expands both on the Mac, so the
    # command ssh carries is literal.
    assert consent_add(server, PLAUD_A).returncode == 0
    host, command = server.log.read_text().splitlines()[:2]
    assert host == "host homelab-test"
    assert command.startswith(
        f"command cd '{server.checkout}' && sh docker/consent-add.sh '{PLAUD_A}'"
    )
    assert "$" not in command
    # local.mk, -include'd, is read from the folder make runs in
    mac = tmp_path / "mac"
    mac.mkdir()
    (mac / "local.mk").write_text(
        "SERVER = homelab-from-local-mk\nREPO_DIR = /srv/example/repo\n", encoding="utf-8"
    )
    makefile = str(REPO / "Makefile")
    dry = subprocess.run(
        ["make", "-n", "-C", str(mac), "-f", makefile, "consent-add", f"ID={PLAUD_A}"],
        env=server.env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    assert dry.returncode == 0, dry.stderr
    assert 'ssh "homelab-from-local-mk" "cd \'/srv/example/repo\' && ' in dry.stdout
    empty = tmp_path / "no-local-mk"
    empty.mkdir()
    refused = subprocess.run(
        ["make", "-n", "-C", str(empty), "-f", makefile, "consent-add", f"ID={PLAUD_A}"],
        env=server.env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    assert refused.returncode != 0 and "local.mk" in refused.stderr
```

```python
def running_backup_guard(tmp_path):
    """deploy-guard.sh against a fake docker whose running backup container is this machine: the
    probe it pipes in runs here, on the test's own lock folder, with the guard's arguments."""
    fake = tmp_path / "docker"
    fake.write_text(
        '#!/bin/sh\nif [ "$1" = ps ]; then echo abc123; exit 0; fi\n'
        'if [ "$1 $2 $3 $4 $5 $6" = "exec -i abc123 python - /state/locks" ]; then\n'
        '  shift 6; exec "$FAKE_PYTHON" - "$FAKE_LOCKS" "$@"\nfi\nexit 99\n',
        encoding="utf-8",
    )
    fake.chmod(0o755)
    env = {
        "PATH": f"{tmp_path}:/usr/bin:/bin",
        "FAKE_PYTHON": sys.executable,
        "FAKE_LOCKS": str(tmp_path / "locks"),
    }

    def guard() -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run(
            ["sh", str(REPO / "docker" / "deploy-guard.sh")],
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            check=False,
        )

    return guard


def announced(job: str) -> str:
    return json.dumps({"job": job, "since": "2026-10-23T12:00:00+00:00"})


def test_the_probe_takes_a_lock_name_and_jobs(tmp_path):
    # why: stage 2b spec §17.3. With jobs given, only a holder that announced one of them counts.
    probe = [sys.executable, str(REPO / "docker" / "ops-busy.py"), str(tmp_path / "locks")]

    def ask(*args: str) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
        return subprocess.run([*probe, *args], capture_output=True, text=True, check=False)

    assert ask().returncode == 2  # a lock name is needed
    assert ask("plaud", "plaud-full").returncode == 0  # never taken
    with ops_lock_held(tmp_path / "locks", announced("plaud-sync"), key="plaud"):
        assert ask("plaud").returncode == 3  # no jobs: any holder counts
        assert ask("plaud", "plaud-full", "plaud-catch-up").returncode == 0  # a routine sync
        assert ask("ops").returncode == 0  # another lock
    with ops_lock_held(tmp_path / "locks", announced("plaud-full"), key="plaud"):
        busy = ask("plaud", "plaud-full", "plaud-catch-up")
        assert busy.returncode == 3 and busy.stdout == announced("plaud-full") + "\n"


def test_the_guard_refuses_for_plaud_full_and_catch_up_and_lets_plaud_sync_through(tmp_path):
    # why: Sync everything, the first catch-up and the baseline run for hours, and a deploy
    # recreates the worker; a routine sync is safe to interrupt (stage 2b spec §17.3).
    guard = running_backup_guard(tmp_path)
    assert guard().returncode == 0
    for job, refused in (
        ("plaud-full", True),
        ("plaud-catch-up", True),
        ("plaud-baseline", True),
        ("plaud-sync", False),
        ("plaud-review", False),
    ):
        with ops_lock_held(tmp_path / "locks", announced(job), key="plaud"):
            done = guard()
            assert (done.returncode != 0) == refused, job
            assert (job in done.stderr and "FORCE=1" in done.stderr) == refused, job
    # the catch-up holds ops too, and announces itself there: the ops question finds it first
    with ops_lock_held(tmp_path / "locks", announced("plaud-catch-up")):
        assert guard().returncode != 0


def test_a_held_plaud_lock_that_cant_be_read_still_refuses(tmp_path):
    # why: a holder between its hold and its announcement, or one whose text is damaged, might be
    # any job: the guard refuses rather than guess.
    guard = running_backup_guard(tmp_path)
    for text in ("", "not json", '["plaud-full"]'):
        with ops_lock_held(tmp_path / "locks", text, key="plaud"):
            done = guard()
            assert done.returncode != 0 and "FORCE=1" in done.stderr, text
```

- [ ] **Step 3: The probe,** `docker/ops-busy.py`, as a whole:

```python
"""Does a job hold a lock now? `ops-busy.py <locks dir> <lock name> [job ...]`: exit 3, printing
what the holder announced, or 0 if the lock is free (2 for a usage error).

docker/deploy-guard.sh pipes this file into the backup container's python
(`python - /state/locks ops`), so it works with whatever image is deployed: standard library only.
A shared, non-blocking flock that fails means another process holds the lock. The probe takes
nothing and lets go at once (as Status does). flock is per host, so a hold in any container counts:
the worker's `plaud` lock is seen from the backup container through the shared state/locks.

With jobs given, only a holder that announced one of them counts (stage 2b spec §17.3: the guard
waits for Sync everything, the catch-up and the baseline, and lets a routine sync be interrupted).
A held lock whose announcement can't be read still counts: it might be any of them.
"""

import errno
import fcntl
import json
import os
import sys


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    if len(argv) < 2:
        print("usage: ops-busy.py <locks dir> <lock name> [job ...]", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    folder, name, jobs = argv[0], argv[1], argv[2:]
    try:
        fd = os.open(os.path.join(folder, f"{name}.lock"), os.O_RDONLY)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return 0  # never taken yet
    try:
        try:
            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_SH | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
        except OSError as exc:
            if exc.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
                raise
        else:
            return 0  # free (closing the descriptor lets go of the probe)
        text = os.pread(fd, 4096, 0).decode("utf-8", "replace").strip()
        if jobs:
            try:
                job = json.loads(text)["job"]
            except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError):
                job = None  # held, but not announced (yet): it might be one of them
            if job is not None and job not in jobs:
                return 0
        print(text or f"{name} is held")
        return 3
    finally:
        os.close(fd)


sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

- [ ] **Step 4: The guard,** `docker/deploy-guard.sh`, as a whole:

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# `make deploy` runs this first. A deploy recreates the backup container, which stops the job it
# runs: restic and rsync stop cleanly, but the job starts again from the beginning, so a deploy
# during a restore test or a check costs hours. While the backup service is stopped (the runbook
# stops it, then runs its jobs and the import in one-off containers), `up` would start the loop in
# their way. It also recreates the worker, which stops a Plaud run: a routine sync is safe to
# interrupt, but Sync everything, the first catch-up and the baseline are long (stage 2b spec
# §17.3). So it asks docker/ops-busy.py, as Status does, whether any process holds the ops lock
# (any job), or the plaud lock for one of those three: in the running backup container, or else in
# a one-off backup container on the image the stopped one was made from (this deploy's image may
# not be built yet). flock is per host, so a hold in any container counts, the worker's included,
# through the shared state/locks. FORCE=1 deploys anyway. It reads no secret.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
[ "${FORCE:-}" = 1 ] && exit 0
ids=$(docker ps -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=recordings \
  --filter label=com.docker.compose.service=backup --filter label=com.docker.compose.oneoff=False) \
  || { echo "deploy-guard: docker failed (is the Docker daemon running?)" >&2; exit 1; }
id=$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | head -n 1)
tag=
if [ -z "$id" ]; then
  # docker ps lists the newest first. The image is read back with inspect, which keeps the
  # reference the container was created from (as docker/up-deployed.sh reads it).
  ids=$(docker ps -a -q --filter label=com.docker.compose.project=recordings \
    --filter label=com.docker.compose.service=backup \
    --filter label=com.docker.compose.oneoff=False) \
    || { echo "deploy-guard: docker failed (is the Docker daemon running?)" >&2; exit 1; }
  stopped=$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | head -n 1)
  [ -n "$stopped" ] || exit 0  # no backup container at all: nothing deployed to stop or start
  image=$(docker inspect --format '{{.Config.Image}}' "$stopped") \
    || { echo "deploy-guard: docker inspect failed (is the Docker daemon running?)" >&2; exit 1; }
  case "$image" in
    recordings:?*) tag=${image#recordings:} ;;
    *) echo "make deploy: could not ask the backup container whether a job is running (it" \
         "runs no image make deploy tagged). make deploy FORCE=1 deploys anyway." >&2
       exit 1 ;;
  esac
fi

# ask <lock name> [job ...]: ops-busy.py's answer (0 free, 3 held), its announcement on stdout.
ask() {
  if [ -n "$id" ]; then
    docker exec -i "$id" python - /state/locks "$@" < docker/ops-busy.py
  else
    RECORDINGS_IMAGE_TAG=$tag docker compose --env-file docker/deploy.env -f docker/compose.yml \
      run --rm --no-deps -T -i backup python - /state/locks "$@" < docker/ops-busy.py
  fi
}

status=0
held=$(ask ops) || status=$?
if [ "$status" = 0 ]; then
  held=$(ask plaud plaud-full plaud-catch-up plaud-baseline) || status=$?
fi
case "$status" in
  0) exit 0 ;;
  3) echo "make deploy: a job is running${held:+ ($held)}. A deploy now would stop it (it would" \
       "start again from the beginning), or start the backup service in its way. Wait for it" \
       "(Status shows it), or deploy anyway: make deploy FORCE=1" >&2 ;;
  *) echo "make deploy: could not ask the backup container whether a job is running (exit" \
       "$status). make deploy FORCE=1 deploys anyway." >&2 ;;
esac
exit 1
```

- [ ] **Step 5: The server's half,** `docker/consent-add.sh` (new, no exec bit: it is run as `sh docker/consent-add.sh`):

```sh
#!/bin/sh
# `make consent-add ID=<id>` runs this on the homelab server, over ssh (stage 2b spec §12.1): it
# adds one Plaud ID to the consent list, as the line "- `<id>` — added <date>". It writes the old
# list and the new line to a new file in the same folder, at the old file's mode, then renames it
# over the list, so the worker, which watches the folder, reads the old list or the new one, never
# half of one. The ID must be 32 hex digits, bare or after `of_`: anything else is refused before
# the list is touched. It reads RECORDINGS_CONSENT_HOST from docker/deploy.env, and no secret.
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
refuse() { echo "consent-add: $1" >&2; exit 2; }
id=${1:-}
case "$id" in
  of_*) hex=${id#of_} ;;
  *) hex=$id ;;
esac
case "$hex" in
  "" | *[!0-9a-fA-F]*) refuse "not a Plaud ID: 32 hex digits, bare or after of_" ;;
esac
[ "${#hex}" -eq 32 ] || refuse "not a Plaud ID: 32 hex digits, bare or after of_"
[ -f docker/deploy.env ] || refuse "docker/deploy.env is missing"
folder=$(sed -n 's/^RECORDINGS_CONSENT_HOST=//p' docker/deploy.env | tail -n 1)
folder=${folder#\"}
folder=${folder%\"}
[ -n "$folder" ] || refuse "RECORDINGS_CONSENT_HOST is not set in docker/deploy.env"
case "$folder" in
  /*) ;;
  *) folder="docker/$folder" ;;  # relative to docker/, as Compose reads it
esac
[ -d "$folder" ] || refuse "$folder (RECORDINGS_CONSENT_HOST) is not a folder"
list="$folder/consent-list.md"
tmp=$(mktemp "$folder/.consent-list.md.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$tmp"' EXIT
perms=rw-------  # a new list: 0600
if [ -f "$list" ]; then
  cat "$list" > "$tmp"
  if [ -s "$tmp" ] && [ -n "$(tail -c 1 "$tmp")" ]; then
    printf '\n' >> "$tmp"  # the old list's last line had no newline
  fi
  perms=$(ls -ln "$list" | cut -c2-10)
fi
printf '%s\n' "- \`$id\` — added $(date +%Y-%m-%d)" >> "$tmp"
u=$(printf '%s' "$perms" | cut -c1-3 | tr -d -)
g=$(printf '%s' "$perms" | cut -c4-6 | tr -d -)
o=$(printf '%s' "$perms" | cut -c7-9 | tr -d -)
chmod "u=$u,g=$g,o=$o" "$tmp"  # the old file's mode, set once the new file is written
mv -f "$tmp" "$list"
echo "consent-add: added $id to $list"
```

- [ ] **Step 6: The Mac's half,** `scripts/consent_id.py` (new; run with `uv run python`, since it imports `recordings`):

```python
"""The one Plaud ID in `make consent-add ID=<text>` (stage 2b spec §12.1), run on the Mac.

    uv run python scripts/consent_id.py '<text>'

<text> is a bare ID, an `of_` ID in any case, or the Sync screen's Copy ID form (`` - `of_…` — ``,
the consent list's own line), read with the consent list's own exclusion rule
(recordings.plaud.keepout.parse_consent), so whatever the list would read as an exclusion is
accepted here and nothing else. It prints the ID's hex as typed, after a lower-case `of_` when it
had one (docker/consent-add.sh takes exactly `(of_)?<32 hex>`), or exits 1 with "not a Plaud ID".
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import re
import sys

from recordings.plaud.keepout import parse_consent
from recordings.refs import canonical_plaud_id

_TYPED = re.compile(r"(?i)(of_)?([0-9a-f]{32})")


def consent_id(text: str) -> str | None:
    if "\n" in text or "\r" in text:
        return None  # one line, one ID
    parsed = parse_consent(text)
    lines = [line for line in parsed.lines if line.kind == "exclusion"]
    found = _TYPED.search(text)
    if len(lines) != 1 or parsed.typo_lines or found is None:
        return None
    typed = ("of_" if found.group(1) else "") + found.group(2)
    return typed if canonical_plaud_id(typed) == lines[0].canonical_id else None


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    found = consent_id(argv[0]) if len(argv) == 1 else None
    if found is None:
        print("consent_id: not a Plaud ID", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    print(found)
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

````markdown
## Keep a recording out for good

Stage 2b's consent list says which Plaud recordings never enter the archive (spec §12.1). Add one:
- **From the Mac:** `make consent-add ID=<id>`, with `SERVER` (your ssh name for the homelab
  server) and `REPO_DIR` (this repo's checkout there) set in `local.mk` at the repo's top
  (git-ignored). `ID` may be the bare ID, the `of_` form, or what the Sync screen's Copy ID puts on
  the clipboard (`` - `of_…` — ``). It checks the ID on the Mac, appends `` - `<id>` — added
  <date> `` on the server by writing a new file and renaming it over the list, and prints what the
  worker reads (`recordings plaud consent`).
- **On the server:** edit `$RECORDINGS_HOME/consent/consent-list.md` with any editor, which writes a
  new file and renames it; the worker watches the folder, so it sees the new file. Then run
  `rc exec worker recordings plaud consent`.

Either way, `recordings plaud consent` must show the new count, and no line it can't read. If your
edit doesn't show, the worker didn't see it. If the recording is already in the archive, the
worker tags it `private` within seconds and flags it; take it out by hand if it mustn't stay.

## Planned work and the sync's check

Planned work doesn't pause the sync's Healthchecks check: re-imports, stopping the worker, or
setting `[plaud] schedule_minutes = 0` for a while. If it lasts more than 2 hours, the check's
email is the reminder to start the worker again or turn the schedule back on, and "up" follows at
the first good sync. Only rolling back across 2b (below), and the final Sync everything when the
Plaud account ends, pause or delete the check, because the sync is then meant to stay off.

## Rolling back across 2b

`make rollback` alone is not enough here: the checkout's `compose.yml` would start a `worker`
whose command the older image lacks. Pause the sync's Healthchecks check first (its Pause button),
because no sync runs until you deploy forward again. Then, on the homelab server, with the top
block pasted:
```bash
rc stop worker && rc rm -f worker
cd "$REPO_DIR"
git checkout <the tag's commit>
make rollback TAG=<tag>
```
`state.db` only gained tables in 2b, and `recording.json` no field, so the older release opens
both. To go forward again, `git checkout` the newer commit, `make deploy`, and resume the check.
````

- [ ] **Step 1: The test scene.** In `packages/ui/tests/conftest.py`, change `from datetime import datetime, timedelta` to `from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta` and `from recordings.archive import Archive` to `from recordings.archive import Archive, RawSource`, then append:

```python
PLAUD_T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 23, 14, 20, tzinfo=UTC)


@dataclass
class PlaudScene:
    """A synthetic archive with a state.db holding the 2b tables, the Plaud cache beside it, and
    the views' settings for them (2b phase 1, Task 19). Rows go in through PlaudDB and Cache.db(),
    as the worker writes them; recordings through the Writer. Synthetic IDs and titles only."""

    writer: Writer
    tmp: Path
    schedule_minutes: int = 20
    auto_import: bool = True
    keep_out_word_ok: bool = True
    added: dict[int, str] = field(default_factory=dict)

    @property
    def db(self):
        from recordings.plaud.checks import PlaudDB

        return PlaudDB(self.writer.state)

    @property
    def settings(self):
        from recordings_ui.plaud import PlaudViewSettings

        return PlaudViewSettings(
            state_path=self.writer.state.path,
            timezone_name="UTC",
            schedule_minutes=self.schedule_minutes,
            full_sweep_days=7,
            auto_import=self.auto_import,
            keep_out_word_ok=self.keep_out_word_ok,
            demo_view=None,
        )

    @staticmethod
    def plaud_id(n: int) -> str:
        return "of_" + f"{n:032x}"  # synthetic

    def add(self, n: int, title: str, tags: tuple[TagRef, ...] = ()) -> str:
        """A recording whose one source is Plaud ID `n`."""
        media = self.tmp / f"plaud-{n}.mp3"
        media.write_bytes(f"ID3 synthetic plaud audio {n}".encode())
        rec = self.writer.add(
            Incoming(
                media=media,
                recorded_at=PLAUD_T0 - timedelta(days=1, minutes=n),
                timezone_name="UTC",
                time_source="metadata",
                title=title,
                kind="audio",
                sources=(
                    RawSource(
                        kind="plaud", ref=self.plaud_id(n), added_at=PLAUD_T0 - timedelta(days=1)
                    ),
                ),
                tags=tags,
            )
        ).recording
        self.added[n] = rec.id
        return rec.id

    def open_gate(self, at: datetime = PLAUD_T0 - timedelta(days=2)) -> None:
        """As the first catch-up leaves it: a snapshot mark and catch_up_done_at (§11.6)."""
        from recordings.plaud.checks import K_CATCH_UP_DONE, K_SNAPSHOT_MARK

        self.db.put_many(
            {
                K_CATCH_UP_DONE: at.isoformat(),
                K_SNAPSHOT_MARK: {"count": 1, "last_at": at.isoformat()},
            },
            now=at,
        )

    def listed(self, at: datetime, count: int = 1, **more) -> None:
        """The last good listing (Phase 2 writes it), as the views read it."""
        from recordings.plaud.checks import K_LAST_GOOD_LISTING

        self.db.put(K_LAST_GOOD_LISTING, {"at": at.isoformat(), "count": count, **more}, now=at)

    def compare(self, rows: list[dict], summary: dict | None = None) -> None:
        """The newest compare in the cache (Phase 2 writes it), replacing the last."""
        from recordings.plaud.cache import Cache

        with Cache(self.writer.state.path).db() as db:
            db.execute("DELETE FROM compare_rows")
            for row in rows:
                full = {
                    "start_at": None,
                    "duration_ms": None,
                    "title": None,
                    "arrives_private": 0,
                    "review": 0,
                    "excluded_by": None,
                    **row,
                }
                db.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO compare_rows (canonical_plaud_id, listed_id, bucket, reason, "
                    "start_at, duration_ms, title, arrives_private, review, excluded_by) "
                    "VALUES (:canonical_plaud_id, :listed_id, :bucket, :reason, :start_at, "
                    ":duration_ms, :title, :arrives_private, :review, :excluded_by)",
                    full,
                )
            db.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO meta (key, value) VALUES ('compare', ?)",
                (json.dumps(summary or {}),),
            )

    def row(self, n: int, bucket: str, reason: str, **more) -> dict:
        return {
            "canonical_plaud_id": f"{n:032x}",
            "listed_id": self.plaud_id(n),
            "bucket": bucket,
            "reason": reason,
            "start_at": (PLAUD_T0 - timedelta(hours=n)).isoformat(),
            "duration_ms": 12 * 60_000,
            **more,
        }


@pytest.fixture
def plaud_scene(writer, tmp_path) -> PlaudScene:
    return PlaudScene(writer, tmp_path)
```

```python
def test_all_here_shows_only_when_true(plaud_scene):
    s = plaud_scene
    s.open_gate()
    s.listed(T0 - timedelta(minutes=30), count=3)
    s.db.put(K_LAST_ENDED, (T0 - timedelta(minutes=5)).isoformat(), now=T0)
    rid = s.add(1, "Week 1")
    s.db.set_check(rid, failures=3, failing_since=(T0 - timedelta(days=1)).isoformat())
    s.db.upsert_listed(s.plaud_id(3), now=T0)
    s.db.set_listing(s.plaud_id(3), parked_at=T0.isoformat(), import_failures=3)
    s.compare([s.row(3, "missing", "failed 3 times")])  # parked: aside (§15.2)
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    assert view["summary"] == {
        "kind": "all-here",
        "sentence": "All here · checked 13:50 · next sync 14:35",
        "explain": ALL_HERE_EXPLAIN,
        "see_status": False,
    }
    panel = sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0)
    assert panel["summary"] == view["summary"]  # one summary, shared (§15)
    # A recording that keeps failing is its own line, and never hides "All here".
    assert "1 recording fails every check (since 2026-10-22)." in panel["conditions"]
    # Two schedule intervals after the last good listing, it isn't shown.
    late = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0 + timedelta(minutes=11), can_request=None)
    assert late["summary"]["kind"] == "problem" and late["summary"]["see_status"] is True
    # Nor with anything waiting.
    s.compare(
        [s.row(3, "missing", "failed 3 times"), s.row(4, "waiting", "imports at the next sync")]
    )
    assert sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)["summary"]["kind"] == "problem"


def test_kept_out_and_flag_rows_carry_no_title(plaud_scene):
    # why: P13. A kept-out or late-flagged recording is shown by ID, date and duration only,
    # whatever a cache row holds, so a title the worker should never have kept can't reach them.
    s = plaud_scene
    s.open_gate()
    rid = s.add(5, "Flagged synthetic 5")
    s.db.upsert_listed(s.plaud_id(5), now=T0)
    s.db.add_event(
        "kept-out-late", now=T0, recording_id=rid, plaud_id=s.plaud_id(5), open_flag=True
    )
    s.compare(
        [
            s.row(
                6, "excluded", "kept out by title", excluded_by="title", title="Kept synthetic 6"
            ),
            s.row(7, "excluded", "on the consent list", excluded_by="consent"),
            s.row(8, "excluded", "on the consent list"),  # no kind: read as the consent list's
        ]
    )
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    shown = json.dumps({"kept_out": view["kept_out"], "flags": view["flags"]})
    assert "synthetic" not in shown.lower()
    assert [(r["by"], r["release"]) for r in view["kept_out"]] == [
        ("title", True),
        ("consent", False),
        ("consent", False),
    ]
    (flag,) = view["flags"]
    assert flag["recording_id"] == rid and flag["keep_here"] is True
    assert flag["sentence"] == SENTENCES["kept-out-late"]
    assert flag["copy_id"] == f"- `{s.plaud_id(5)}` —"


def test_not_here_titles_come_from_the_cache_and_hide_with_its_reason(plaud_scene):
    s = plaud_scene
    s.open_gate()
    s.compare(
        [
            s.row(
                8, "waiting", "imports at the next sync", title="Synthetic 042", arrives_private=1
            ),
            s.row(
                9,
                "missing",
                "needs your review: the sync's records were rebuilt",
                title="Synthetic 043",
                review=1,
            ),
        ]
    )
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    rows = {r["plaud_id"]: r for r in view["not_here"]}
    assert rows[s.plaud_id(8)]["title"] == "Synthetic 042"
    assert rows[s.plaud_id(8)]["arrives_private"] is True
    assert rows[s.plaud_id(8)]["copy_id"] == f"- `{s.plaud_id(8)}` —"
    assert (rows[s.plaud_id(8)]["date"], rows[s.plaud_id(8)]["time"]) == ("2026-10-23", "06:20")
    assert rows[s.plaud_id(8)]["duration"] == "12 min"
    assert rows[s.plaud_id(9)]["title"] is None and rows[s.plaud_id(9)]["review"] is True
    assert view["import_all"] == {"count": 1, "review_more": 1}
    hidden = "titles hidden while Plaud's IDs look changed"
    s.compare(
        [s.row(8, "waiting", "imports at the next sync", title="Synthetic 042")],
        {"titles_hidden": hidden},
    )
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    assert view["titles_hidden"] == hidden and view["not_here"][0]["title"] is None
    s.compare([s.row(8, "waiting", "imports at the next sync", title="Synthetic 042")])
    open_blocker(s.db, "consent", now=T0)
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    assert view["titles_hidden"] == TITLES_HIDDEN_CONSENT and view["not_here"][0]["title"] is None
    # Imported since the compare: here now (its title hash is kept), so its row goes.
    s.add(8, "Synthetic 042")
    s.db.upsert_listed(s.plaud_id(8), now=T0)
    s.db.set_listing(s.plaud_id(8), title_sha256="0" * 64)
    assert sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)["not_here"] == []


def test_the_not_pinged_line_names_the_cause_from_sync_health(plaud_scene):
    # C6.06: an error shows from the first failed run, though Healthchecks emails only about 2
    # hours later, and the not-pinged line names what stopped the ping, from sync_health().
    s = plaud_scene
    s.open_gate()
    pinged = T0 - timedelta(minutes=40)
    s.db.put(K_LAST_PING, {"at": pinged.isoformat(), "ok": True, "status": 200}, now=pinged)
    failed = T0 - timedelta(minutes=20)
    record_run(
        s.db,
        RunOutcome(
            listing="none", attempts=0, successes=0, disk_refused=False, detail="sign-in needed"
        ),
        now=failed,
    )
    open_blocker(s.db, "sign-in", now=failed)
    panel = sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0)
    assert panel["not_pinged"] == (
        "The sync's Healthchecks check isn't being pinged since 13:40: sign-in needed. "
        "It emails you about 2 hours after that."
    )
    assert panel["failing"].startswith("Plaud sync failing since 14:00 (")
    assert panel["conditions"][0].startswith("Plaud sign-in needed since 14:00. ")
    assert panel["numbers"]["healthchecks"] == "last pinged 13:40"
    # One schedule interval plus 10 minutes after the last ping, and not before.
    assert sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0 - timedelta(minutes=11))["not_pinged"] is None


def test_the_schedule_off_for_24_hours_after_the_catch_up_needs_attention(plaud_scene):
    # C6.14. Off before the catch-up is plain; after it, once off for 24 hours, Needs attention.
    s = plaud_scene
    s.schedule_minutes = 0
    before = sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0)
    assert "Scheduled sync is off." in before["conditions"]
    assert not [a for a in before["attention"] if a.startswith("Scheduled sync")]
    done = T0 - timedelta(hours=30)
    s.open_gate(at=done)
    early = sync_panel(s.settings, now=done + timedelta(hours=23))
    assert "Scheduled sync is off since 2026-10-22 08:20." in early["conditions"]
    assert not [a for a in early["attention"] if a.startswith("Scheduled sync")]
    late = sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0)
    assert [a for a in late["attention"] if a.startswith("Scheduled sync")] == [
        (
            "Scheduled sync has been off since 2026-10-22 08:20: set [plaud] schedule_minutes to "
            "turn it back on, or pause the sync's Healthchecks check (runbook)."
        )
    ]


def test_each_needs_attention_entry_phase_1_can_show(plaud_scene):
    s = plaud_scene
    s.schedule_minutes = 0
    s.open_gate(at=T0 - timedelta(hours=30))
    db = s.db
    db.put(K_CONSENT, {"ids": 3, "stop": typo_phrase([14, 22]), "read_at": T0.isoformat()}, now=T0)
    open_blocker(db, "consent", now=T0 - timedelta(minutes=5))
    a, b, c = s.add(11, "Week 11"), s.add(12, "Week 12"), s.add(13, "Week 13")
    db.add_event("consent-late", now=T0, recording_id=a, plaud_id=s.plaud_id(11), open_flag=True)
    db.add_event("kept-out-late", now=T0, recording_id=b, plaud_id=s.plaud_id(12), open_flag=True)
    db.add_event("private-unwritten", now=T0, recording_id=c, open_flag=True)
    db.upsert_listed(s.plaud_id(14), now=T0)
    db.set_listing(s.plaud_id(14), needs_review=1)
    beat = T0 - timedelta(minutes=10)
    heartbeat_once(s.writer.state, Progress(phase="idle", counter=1, at=beat), now=beat)
    failed_since = T0 - timedelta(hours=2, minutes=1)
    db.put(
        K_LAST_PING,
        {
            "at": (T0 - timedelta(minutes=5)).isoformat(),
            "ok": False,
            "status": 404,
            "failed_since": failed_since.isoformat(),
        },
        now=T0,
    )
    with plaud_run(s.writer.state, "plaud-sync", timeout=1.0, now=T0 - timedelta(hours=3)):
        attention = sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0)["attention"]
    for line in (
        (
            "Plaud imports stopped: the consent list has 2 lines that look like IDs but can't be "
            "read (lines 14 and 22)."
        ),
        f"Recording {a} is on the consent list, but in the archive. Take it out by hand (runbook).",
        (
            f"Recording {b} was kept out by title after it came in. Take it out by hand (runbook), "
            "or Keep it here."
        ),
        (
            f"Recording {c} should be private, but its file was edited outside the app: run "
            "`recordings reindex`."
        ),
        "The sync's records were rebuilt: 1 recording waits for your review on the Sync screen.",
        (
            "The Plaud worker is silent (last reported 14:10): check that the worker container is "
            "running."
        ),
        "A sync has run since 11:20: it may be stuck.",
        PING_FAILING,
    ):
        assert line in attention, line
    assert [x for x in attention if x.startswith("Scheduled sync has been off since")]
    # Sync everything may hold the lock for 12 hours before it may be stuck.
    with plaud_run(s.writer.state, "plaud-full", timeout=1.0, now=T0 - timedelta(hours=3)):
        attention = sync_panel(s.settings, now=T0)["attention"]
    assert not [x for x in attention if x.endswith("it may be stuck.")]


def test_with_the_gate_closed_every_button_but_compare_says_why(plaud_scene):
    s = plaud_scene
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    assert view["available"] is True and view["reason"] is None
    assert view["buttons"] == {
        "sync": GATE_FIRST,
        "compare": None,
        "full": GATE_FIRST,
        "import": GATE_FIRST,
    }
    why = "there's no config.toml, so this app only reads the archive"
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=why)
    assert view["available"] is False and view["buttons"] == dict.fromkeys(view["buttons"], why)
    # Under a hold the import buttons say the hold's line; Sync now answers "Held: see Status".
    s.open_gate()
    held = "Plaud now lists 40 fewer of the recordings here (and 38 look new)."
    s.db.put(K_HOLD, {"sentence": held}, now=T0)
    open_blocker(s.db, "hold", now=T0)
    view = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0, can_request=None)
    assert view["buttons"] == {"sync": None, "compare": None, "full": None, "import": held}
    assert view["hold"] == {"sentence": held, "accept": True, "refused": None}


def test_the_demo_view_is_the_hand_written_fixture_with_the_demo_notes(tmp_path):
    raw = json.loads(DEMO_FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    view = demo_view(DEMO_FIXTURE)
    sync, panel = view["sync"], view["panel"]
    # Every key is written, and none is misspelt.
    assert set(raw["sync"]) == set(sync) and set(raw["panel"]) == set(panel)
    assert (sync["demo"], sync["available"], sync["reason"]) == (True, False, DEMO_NOTE)
    assert sync["summary"]["kind"] == "demo" and sync["summary"]["sentence"] == DEMO_NOTE
    assert set(sync["buttons"].values()) == {DEMO_NOTE}
    assert sync["not_here"] == [{**row, "park": False} for row in raw["sync"]["not_here"]]
    assert not [r for r in sync["kept_out"] if r["release"]]
    assert not [f for f in sync["flags"] if f["keep_here"]]
    assert panel["summary"]["sentence"] == DEMO_STATUS and panel["attention"] == []
    assert view["arrivals"] == raw["arrivals"]
    # Hand-written and synthetic: every Plaud ID is a small counter.
    ids = re.findall(r"of_[0-9a-f]+", DEMO_FIXTURE.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    assert ids and all(re.fullmatch(r"of_0{24}[0-9a-f]{8}", i) for i in ids)
    # Demo mode copies it beside the archive's copy, where the views read it (decision 23).
    canned = demo_view_settings(from_env({}, demo=True).archive)
    assert canned.demo_view.read_bytes() == DEMO_FIXTURE.read_bytes()
    assert sync_view(canned, now=T0, can_request="any reason") == sync
    assert sync_panel(canned, now=T0) == panel
    assert arrivals(canned, since=T0, now=T0) == view["arrivals"]
    assert recording_plaud(canned, "19620912T100000-0500_229ce3ea", now=T0) is None
    assert status_view(tmp_path, None, now=T0, plaud=canned)["sync"] == panel
    # A missing file is an empty canned view, never an error: the demo still starts.
    empty = demo_view(tmp_path / "missing.json")
    assert empty["sync"]["not_here"] == [] and empty["sync"]["buttons"]["compare"] == DEMO_NOTE

    s = plaud_scene

def test_arrivals_count_events_since_and_flags_by_count_only(plaud_scene):
    s = plaud_scene
    db = s.db
    since = T0 - timedelta(hours=1)
    db.add_event(
        "imported", now=since - timedelta(minutes=1), recording_id="20261023T120000+0000_0000beef"
    )
    for i, kind in enumerate(
        ("imported", "imported", "arrived-private", "updated", "retagged-private")
    ):
        db.add_event(
            kind, now=T0 - timedelta(minutes=10), recording_id=f"20261023T14{i:02d}00+0000_0000beef"
        )
    a, b = s.add(21, "Week 21"), s.add(22, "Week 22")
    db.add_event("kept-out-late", now=T0, recording_id=a, plaud_id=s.plaud_id(21), open_flag=True)
    db.add_event("consent-late", now=T0, recording_id=b, plaud_id=s.plaud_id(22), open_flag=True)
    counts = arrivals(s.settings, since=since, now=T0)
    assert counts == {"new": 2, "private": 1, "updated": 2, "kept_out_late": 1, "consent_late": 1}
    assert {type(v) for v in counts.values()} == {int}  # counts only: no title, no ID
    # A Refresh moves `since`: what came before it no longer counts; the flags still do.
    assert arrivals(s.settings, since=T0, now=T0) == {**ZERO, "kept_out_late": 1, "consent_late": 1}
    assert arrivals(None, since=since, now=T0) == ZERO

def test_the_plaud_views_import_on_pyodide_without_sqlite(demo_archive):
    # why: the Pages demo runs recordings_ui on Pyodide, which has no sqlite3 (tagging.py,
    # status.py). Its views draw only the canned view, and must not import what reads state.db.
    code = (
        "import sys; from datetime import UTC, datetime; from pathlib import Path; "
        "import recordings_ui.plaud as p; import recordings_ui.status as st; "
        f"s = p.demo_view_settings(Path({str(demo_archive)!r})); now = datetime.now(UTC); "
        "p.sync_view(s, now=now, can_request=None); p.sync_panel(s, now=now); "
        "p.arrivals(s, since=now, now=now); p.recording_plaud(s, 'x', now=now); "
        "st.status_view(Path('.'), None, plaud=s); "
        "print(sorted(m for m in ('sqlite3', 'recordings.state', 'recordings.writer', "
        "'recordings.plaud.checks') if m in sys.modules))"
    )
    out = subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-c", code], capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
    assert out.stdout.strip() == "[]"
```

```python
def _status_settings(state_path) -> StatusSettings:
    return StatusSettings(
        state_path=state_path, timezone_name="UTC", warn=20.0, stop=5.0, jobs=("disk",)
    )


def test_status_never_carries_a_title(plaud_scene):
    # why: P13 and §15.2. Status names recordings by ID; the Sync screen alone may name them, from
    # the cache (not here yet) and from the recording here.
    s = plaud_scene
    s.open_gate()
    s.listed(T0_SYNC - timedelta(minutes=10), count=2)
    rid = s.add(2, "Private synthetic title 2")
    s.db.add_event(
        "updated",
        now=T0_SYNC - timedelta(minutes=5),
        recording_id=rid,
        plaud_id=s.plaud_id(2),
        detail={"parts": ["title"]},
    )
    s.db.add_event(
        "kept-out-late", now=T0_SYNC, recording_id=rid, plaud_id=s.plaud_id(2), open_flag=True
    )
    s.compare([s.row(3, "waiting", "imports at the next sync", title="Cached synthetic title 3")])
    settings = _status_settings(s.writer.state.path)
    view = status_view(s.writer.root, settings, now=T0_SYNC, plaud=s.settings)
    assert view["sync"]["no_sync_yet"] is False
    assert any(rid in line for line in view["attention"])  # by ID
    assert "synthetic title" not in json.dumps(view).lower()
    screen = sync_view(s.settings, now=T0_SYNC, can_request=None)
    assert screen["not_here"][0]["title"] == "Cached synthetic title 3"
    assert screen["updated"][0]["title"] == "Private synthetic title 2"


def test_without_the_2b_tables_it_says_no_sync_has_run_yet_never_the_restore_text(plaud_scene):
    # why: §9.5. A state.db from before 2b, or a release rolled back to, has no 2b tables. That
    # is "No sync has run yet", never a damaged state.db: restoring a sound one loses its queue.
    s = plaud_scene
    rid = s.add(1, "Week 1")
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(s.writer.state.db_path)) as conn, conn:
        for table in PLAUD_TABLES:
            conn.execute(f"DROP TABLE {table}")
    settings = _status_settings(s.writer.state.path)
    view = status_view(s.writer.root, settings, now=T0_SYNC, plaud=s.settings)
    assert view["sync"]["no_sync_yet"] is True
    assert view["sync"]["summary"]["sentence"] == NO_SYNC_YET
    assert not [line for line in view["attention"] if "restore" in line]
    assert sync_view(s.settings, now=T0_SYNC, can_request=None)["summary"]["kind"] == "no-sync"
    assert set(arrivals(s.settings, since=T0_SYNC, now=T0_SYNC).values()) == {0}
    # Details still names its Plaud ID, for `make consent-add`.
    lines = recording_plaud(s.settings, rid, now=T0_SYNC)
    assert lines["plaud_ids"] == [{"id": s.plaud_id(1), "copy_id": f"- `{s.plaud_id(1)}` —"}]
    assert lines["checked"] is None
```
